**Dharmakuta, Rituals performed on the birth of a son: 1.18.18-19**

**Комментарий:**

A holy day is not a day of festivity. Nor is a festive day a holy day. The day of the son’s birth, however, is both holy and festive. Vyasa also agrees, ‘When a son is born to a brahmin both gods and manes arrive (to participate in the ceremonies and festivities). Therefore, that day is both ‘holy and festive’, the day when the father gives away gold, land, cows, horses, chariots, umbrellas, fragrant substances, etc. The gods and manes who arrive on that occasion are gratified through Jateshti (a ceremony performed for the birth of a child) and Vriddhishraddha (an offering made on the occasion) respectively. Bodhayana ordains offerings of ‘twelve cups of ghee’ to the manes when a son is born’. The Vishnupurana says, ‘When a son is born, the father should be given an oil-bath. Jatakarma along with shraddha should then be performed.

Gifts on the birth of a son:

Presentations are made to brahmins, kings and entertainers on happy occasions ‘Gifts to brahmins for piety and to dancers for fame’ says the Mahabharata. They are called gifts for pleasure by scholars of Dharmasastra, points out Devala in Madhaviya.

In Ayodhyakanda, Kausalya gives gold, cows, and gems to the bringer of good news of Rāma’s coronation. Similarly in Sundarakanda, Rāma says to Hanumat who reported on his having found Sita, ‘However, helpless I am to offer anything equally pleasing to this messenger of the happy news, I am extremely pained at heart. I shall only return the embrace I received from Hanumat. May that serve the purpose for the time being’. Similarly, when Hanumat brought the happy news of Rāma’s victory over Ravana Sita says, ‘O Hanuman, I cannot think of any gift to reciprocate the joy you have brought me. Gold or gems of various kinds or even the kingdom of the three worlds will not be worthy of this happiness’. In the same kanda, when Hanuman brought the news of Rāma’s return to the capital after killing Ravana, Bharata replies, ‘I wonder whether you are a god or a human being. I offer you a hundred thousand cows, hundreds of villages, sixteen virtuous brides’.

Thus there is no day like the day of a son’s birth which is worthy of celebrations according to both Shrutis and Smritis. What is more than this is the report. Which is a penance in a verbal form as it is pleasing, beneficial and true. The Gita says, ‘A report which is true, pleasing and beneficial is an oral penance’. ‘When the messenger from the ladies’ apartment ‘brought the news of the birth of a son, writes Kalidasa, ‘there were only three things which the king could not give him viz. the royal canopy white like the moon and the two chowries’.

## Summary Sarga 18

The ritual consecrations of the asvamedha ended. The gods received their share of the havis and returned to their worlds. The happy Lords and rulers of the earth went back to their countries while Dasaratha returned to Ayodhya with his queens and entourage. Rsyasringa and Santa took leave of the king who now awaited the birth of his sons. Six seasons passed after the completion of the rituals. In the month of Chaitra on the ninth day of the new Moon, in Karkata lagna presided by Aditi as devata, when the star Punarvasu was in ascendance, with the five planets Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus, Kausalya gave birth to an illustrious son, Rāma. She beheld him, with great joy. Blessed with every sign of divinity, he was one half of Visnu. Kaikeyi’s son, Bharata, was born under the next star Pushya, which was ascendant in the Meena lagna. To Sumitra were born the equally impeccable Lakshmana and Satrughna in the Karkata lagna when the star Aslesha appeared. These incarnations of Visnu as the four sons of Dasaratha radiated effulgence like the stars of Purvabhadra and Uttarabhadra. At that auspicious moment the palace reverberated with joy. Gandharvas sang, apsaras danced, the kettledrums of heaven boomed and the skies rained flowers. The streets of Ayodhya reverberated with the sound of music as the citizens celebrated the birth of the divine princes with joy. Twelve days after, Vasishta performed appropriate rituals and named the first-born Rāma, Kaikeyi's son, Bharata and Sumitra’s twins, Lakshmana and Satrughna. The brahmins were feted, feasted and showered with gifts and the people of Ayodhya came in droves from towns and country to share the joy of the palace.

The sons of Dasaratha, who soon learnt the Vedas, were virtuous, valiant, and ever concerned about the welfare of the people. Among them Rāma, devout, dedicated and free of all taint endeared himself to the entire world and was Dasaratha’s most beloved son. Lakshmana, who loved Rāma more than his life, followed him like his shadow. Rāma too reciprocated his brother’s love. Bharata and Satrughna also had a strong bond between them. Though Dasaratha took great pride in them, the princes never took advantage of his affection and were ever ready to serve him with love and reverence. Renowned for their great knowledge, wisdom and virtue, they were yet modest and aware of the ways of the world.

One day while Dasaratha was conferring with his ministers and kinsmen, Viswamitra, the mighty ascetic, arrived at the gates of the palace commanding the guards to inform the king that Viswamitra, son of Kusika, was seeking to meet him and quivering with excitement Dasaratha along with Vasishta hastened to welcome Viswamitra.

Here one may like to know how the seer knows Rāma to be the embodiment of the Supreme Self. The Shruti clearly asserts, ‘One who does not know, knows it. He, who knows it, knows it not” (KenaU 2.3). To this, we say that all the Shrutis negate the complete knowledge of the Paramatman. Speech returns with the mind without attaining the Brahman’.

## Summary Sarga 19

Touched by Dasaratha’s warm words of welcome, Viswamitra said, “Engaged in performing certain rituals I am facing great hindrances from the rakshasas, including Maricha and Subahu who have been raining flesh and blood on the sacrificial altar. These demons whose magical powers allow them to take any form at will disrupt my austerities. I cannot unleash my wrath upon them for anger will destroy the merit earned through my penance. So give me Rāma, your first-born, who knows no fear. He alone with his divine radiance is capable of slaying the rakshasas and I shall spread his fame in all the three worlds. Maricha and Subahu are of no match for Rāma. They can never face him! Deem them dead already! I know of Rāma’s boundless courage and might, Vasishta will bear with me. If your dharma and your fame are to remain forever on earth, give me Rāma for ten nights. Let not the auspicious time set for my ritual slip away.” Viswamitra fell silent, while Dasaratha, shattered and frightened sat on his throne trembling.

## Sarga 20

## On king Dasaratha’s refusal

\[On king Dasaratha’s refusal to accede to his request, Viswamitra gets enraged.\]

### Verse 1.20.1

*tacchrutva rajasardrlo visvamitrasya bhasitam*  
*muhrrtamiva nissanjnassanjnavanidamabravit*

**Перевод:**

**On hearing Viswamitra, words the tiger among kings (Dasaratha) lost his senses for a moment and on regaining his consciousness spoke this way:**  
**Tilaka, Dasaratha’s rejection of Viswamitra’s proposal 1.20.1**

**Комментарий:**

Dasaratha fell unconscious due to the fear of the demons, in case he conceded Viswamitra’s proposal. He argued that his son was less than sixteen years of age and hence he was unfit to fight. I will fight as a master of the army tells Dasaratha and offers himself. As a young boy and being below sixteen Dasaratha thought Rāma was still boyish and that Dasaratha though old is still strong enough to fight. ‘Among my four sons I have the greatest love for Rāma’ says Dasaratha. Among the three purusarthas, dharma is involved while fighting against demons. When dharma is forgotten while fighting then the kingdom itself may disintegrate, as there could be no rule of the kingdom without dharma. Therefore, Rāma cannot be sent. The king then asks the kind of demons that Rāma has to fight in order to stress that Rāma is completely unfit for the task. He asks “How formidable are they in their appearance? Who are their guardians? How are they to be countered? How can they be slain”. Viswamitra tells Dasaratha that among the demons Ravana is quite famous. Provoked by Ravana the two demons Marica and Subhahu are causing hindrances to the sacrifice. On hearing the name of Ravana the king lost all hope of fighting against that demon: “Even accompanied by the army and my sons I cannot fight the demons. Maybe, you have the confidence but I cannot send my sons, Rāma may appear like a god but he is, in reality, not” said Dasaratha.

Marica and Subhahu born to Sunda and Upasunda through a yaksha are like fire. They had turned demons due to Agastya’s curse.

### Verse 1.20.2

*rnasodasavarso me ramo rajivalocanah*  
*na yuddhayogyatamasya pasyami saha raksasaih*

**Перевод:**

**“My lotus-eyed son Rāma is less than sixteen. I do not think he has ability to fight with the demons in a battle.**  
**Siromani, Rāma’s age at exile 1.20.2**

**Комментарий:**

The lotus-eyed Rāma is less than sixteen. That is, he has just completed fifteen years and has entered into the sixteenth at the time of his departure with Vālmīki. Marica later on says, ‘Sixteen-year-old Rāma is not a consummate archer.’ Further, we can conclude that Rāma was twenty-eight at the time of his exile. This is supported by Sita’s statement, ‘I lived for twelve years in Raghava’s abode my brilliant husband is twenty-eight.’ Kausalya also exclaims, ‘O son, twenty-eight years have passed after your birth!’.

On the other hand, it may be argued that Rāma was twenty-five at the time of his exile. Here, Sita’s panca-vimsaka is taken in literal sense, i.e. ‘of twenty-five’. Other events confirm this. At the time of his departure with Viswamitra, Rāma was quarter to sixteen, i.e. twelve years. He married Sita at thirteen. And Sita spent twelve years in Rāma’s palace before exile.

Bhusanakara is of the same opinion. However, he reckons the period in a different way. He takes Kausalya’s expression dasa sapta ca varsani meaning, literally, seventeen years. He calculates this period from Rāma’s upanayana, the second birth of the twice-born castes. He presumes that the upanayana commenced in his eighth year and adds ‘eight’ to ‘seventeen’. In our view, the opinion deserves consideration, since the age is sometimes counted either from birth or from upanayana.

### Verse 1.20.3

*iyamaksauhini prrna yasyaham patirisvarah*  
*anaya samvrto gatva yoddha'ham tairnisacaraih*

**Перевод:**

**“Here is the whole akshauhini (army) of which I am the Lord and sustainer. Accompanied by the akshauhini I shall engage those rakshasas in the battle.**  
**Amritakataka, Explanation of Akshauhini 1.20.3**

**Комментарий:**

The term Akshauhini denotes the large number of warriors in an army. The specifics are detailed in Adiparva of the Mahabharata. One chariot, one elephant, three horses and five-foot soldiers put together are called patti. Three pattis make one senamukha, three senamukhas, one gulma, three gulmas, one gana, three ganas, one vahini, three vahinis, one prtana, three prtanass one camu, three camus, one anikini, and ten anikinis, one aksauhini.

'I am keeper and master of such an army. I shall go with this aksauhini army and fight with those raksasas who ravage your yajna' tells Dasaratha to Viswamitra.

Siromani, *Aksauhini* 1.20.3

Dasaratha said to Viswamitra, “Seer, I am the guardian and the chief of aksauhini army. I will send them to fight night-roving demons that spoil your sacrifices.” This indicates that there is no need to send Rāma.

The Adiparvan of the Mahabharata states the formation of the aksauhini army, thus: The ‘Patti’ is the smallest division of an army consisting of one chariot, one elephant, three horsemen, and five army-men. Three ‘pattis’ form the senamukha, the van of an army. The gulma, the guard of soldiers, consists of three senamukhas. Three gulmas form the gana, the body of troops, while three ganas evolve the vahini. Three vahinis constitute the prtana, the hostile armament. Three prtanas yield camu. Three Camus form an anikini. Last, the ten anikinis constitute the aksauhini.

*ityukto munina tena rajovaca munim tada*  
*na hi sakto'smi sangrame sthatum tasya duratmanah*

### Verse 1.20.21

*sa tvam prasadam dharmajna! kurusva mama putrake*  
*mama caivalpabhagyasya daivatam hi bhavanguruh*

**Перевод:**

**“You are the knower of righteousness. Be kind to my little son and also to me for I am so unfortunate. You are verily my preceptor and god.**  
**Siromani, Dasaratha’s plea to Viswamitra 1.20.21**

**Комментарий:**

Dasaratha, again, asserts his inability to offer a battle against Ravana. He pleads when we learn that the gods could not combat with Ravana in the battlefield, we would not resist him. Thus here is the figure of speech kavyarthapatti. It further implies that when all are too incompetent to rival Ravana, it naturally follows that I cannot endure him. The same figure of speech reveals another kavyarthapatti. Furthermore, the passing reference to Brahma’s grant of the boon in Viswamitra's speech suggests that the king has ascertained Ravana’s invulnerability.

The expression nasaktosm indicates Dasaratha’s want of urge to present himself at the seer’s place. It reveals Dasaratha’s reflection, thus: On hearing the defeat of Marica and Subahu, Ravana would surely arrive there. However, the king would not kill him, since his slaughter would cause Brahma’s disrespect. This, further, shows Dasaratha’s awareness of moral conduct.

“Marica and Subahu, sons of Sund and Upasund, interrupt your sacrifice. They are terrible like Kala or the God of Death in the battlefield. Certainly, I will not allow Rāma to join you.” Dasaratha means to say that the demons with mightiest limbs are adept at their vicious tricks. On the contrary, Rāma has a tender body. He is not fit to fight them. According to a maxim, “Both wedding and disputing with the equals are commendable. Marica and Subahu, the famous descendants of the family of daityas, are brave. Born to the yaksa-kanya, they are trained well in warfare. They attained demoniac nature owing to Agastya’s curse. I will join you with the host of my allies to fight against any of your enemy stronger than Marica and Subahu. However, I will surely join you with my kinsmen even if there is no occasion for combat.”

Here the content conveys the following ideas: 1. The particle ca recalls Agastya’s curse. 2. Dasaratha would not fight with Marica and Subahu. 3. Their birth in demon’s family hints their relation with Ravana, the recipient of Brahma’s boon. 4. Born to yaksa-kanya, they belonged to yaksa family. The king remembered Manu’s words addressed to Dhruva, stating ''yakshas should not be killed.” Their slaughter would lead to Manu’s disrespect. All these facts forced the king’s unwillingness to join the seer.

Tilaka, Rāma’s Age 1.20.21

How old was Rāma when he accompanied Viswamitra? Was he a little less than sixteen years (as Dasaratha tells Viswamitra) or was he only twelve years as Marica described him. According to Kataka, ‘only a kshatriya prince who has completed sixteen years can wear armour and fight’. Kataka believes that in order to create fear in Ravana, Marica must have referred to Rāma as a twelve-year-old in an exaggerated way.

### Verse 1.20.22

*devadanavagandharva yaksa: patagapannagah*  
*na sakta ravanam sodhum kim punarmanava yudhi*

**Перевод:**

## Summary Sarga 20

Emerging from his daze, Dasaratha said, “Rāma is not even sixteen. Is it possible for him to war with the rakshasas? I have an entire akshauhini of which I am the Lord and master. I shall go to war with those armies for they and not Rāma can vanquish the enemy. With bow in hand so long as there is life in me I shall protect the yajna and fight Maricha and Subahu. Rāma is but a mere boy, inexperienced in war and in the wielding of weapons. He is no match for the rakshasas who are notorious for their treachery. Separated from Rāma, I cannot live! Born to me after sixty thousand years, he is my greatest delight, so do spare him” Dasaratha then wanted to know more about the rakshasas, “What are their powers? Who are they and whose sons are they? What kind of bodies do they have and how does one counter their treachery? Neither Rāma nor I can match their magical powers, or ward off their evil because these creatures are justly proud of being invincible. Great Brahmin, how can Rāma oppose these deceitful demons?” and Viswamitra said, “Maricha and Subahu are disrupting my yaga at the behest of Ravana”.

Dasaratha said, “I have not the strength to confront Ravana. Viswamitra! you are my guru and my god, be gracious. When even the devas, danavas, yakshas and pannagas cannot face Ravana, how can men match him? How can I send my son to fight those monsters who seem the very incarnations of death?" When Viswamitra heard Dasaratha, he exploded into a terrible rage, blazing like the flames of a sacrificial fire fed by oblations!

## Sarga 21

## On Vasistha’s advice

\[On Vasistha’s advice, Dasaratha agrees to send Rāma with Viswamitra.\]

### Verse 1.21.1

*tacchrutva vacanam tasya snehaparyakulaksaram*  
*samanyuh kausiko vakyam pratyuvaca mahipatim*

**Перевод:**

**On hearing his words full of contradictions out of affection for his son, Dasaratha replied to the enraged Viswamitra:**  
**Dharmakuta, Reputation of the Ikshvakus as donors: 1.21.1-2**

**Комментарий:**

It was the sacred duty of the kings of the Ikshvaku race, not to send a supplicant away with his wish unfulfilled. Saubhari says in the Vishnupurana, “O king, I wish to marry your daughter. Give her to me. Do not shatter my love. Never do supplicants coming to the kings of the race of Kakutstha with a request go disappointed. O Mandhatar, yours is the only glorious family with a vow, as it were, to fulfil the desires of the supplicants”.

Kalidasa reiterates the same: “Let there be no new accusation that a supplicant asking for dakshina to be given to his guru went away to another donor from Raghu who could not fulfil his desire”.

Siromani, Breach of promise considered as an unrighteous act 1.21.1-8

Dasaratha’s speech was brimming over with affection. It showed the impracticability of Rāma’s going with the seer. On hearing it, the wrathful seer said to the king: “First you promised to fulfil my wish. Now you withdraw your words. The breach of promise does not befit you, born in Raghava’s lineage. It exposes your untruthfulness. People will lay blame on you, saying that a liar is born in the family of the truthful. As I arrive, I will go back to my hermitage unaccompanied by Rāma”.

The threat actually implies Viswamitra’s insistence on having Rāma with him. No sooner did Viswamitra, the steady and furious seer, utter these words than the whole earth ruled by him began to tremble. Even the gods were frightened. The statement suggests four ideas. 1. Viswamitra was endowed with great prowess. 2. The gods thought that the seer who was irate with his friend Dasaratha might be angry with them. 3. The earth’s trembling implies the fear of the mother earth. 4. The seer’s wrath was not real, but just contrived. It merely aimed at frightening the king.

### Verse 1.21.2

*prrvamartham pratisrutya pratijnam hatumicchasi*  
*raghavanamayukto'yam kulasyasya viparyayah*

**Перевод:**

**“First you made a promise and (now) you want to break it. This is highly improper for a descendant of Raghus dynasty”.**

### Verse 1.21.3

*yadidam te ksamam rajan! gamisyami yatha'gatam*  
*mithyapratijnah kakutstha! sukhibhava sabandhavah*

**Перевод:**

**If this act of yours is appropriate to you, O king, I will go back (to the place) wherefrom I came. O scion of the race of kakutstha, you have proved false to your promise. Live happily with your relatives”.**  
**Dharmakuta, Preceptor must advise the king swerving from the right path 1.21.3-20**

**Комментарий:**

When out of affection for his son Dasaratha refuses to fulfil his promise, Vasistha, realizes that Viswamitra’s fury would create havoc in the entire world. So he intervenes. He explains to the king the principle of propriety with a desire to avert the destruction of everything including Dasaratha’s acts of charity.

‘Ministers should restrain the king’, states Kamandaka, ‘from doing an improper act’. ‘Ministers’, he continues, ‘who stop the king swerving from the right path are not just friends. They are his great gurus'.

### Verse 1.21.4

*tasya rosaparitasya visvamitrasya dhimatah*  
*cacala vasudha krtsna .ivesa .a bhayam .uran*

**Перевод:**

**At the sight of the wise sage Viswamitra in rage, the entire earth shook and devatas were gripped in fear.**

### Verse 1.21.5

*trastarrpam tu vijnaya jagatsarvam mahanrsih*  
*nrpatim suvrato dhiro vasistho vakyamabravit*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the entire world frightened, great Vasistha, an adherent of ascetic practices and steadfast (to duty), said to the king:**

### Verse 1.21.6

*iksvakrnam kule jatassaksaddharma ivaparah*  
*dhrtiman suvratah srimannadharmam hatumarhasi*

**Перевод:**

*trisu lokesu vikhyato dharmatma iti raghava*  
*svadharmam pratipadyasva nadharmam vodhumarhasi*

**Перевод:**

**“O Dasaratha! you are reputed in the three worlds as righteous-minded. Do your own duty. Do not follow an unjust act which is unworthy of respect.**

### Verse 1.21.8

*samsrutyaivam karisyamityakurvanasya raghava*  
*istaprrtavadho bhryattasmadramam visarjaya*

**Перевод:**

**“O Dasaratha, a promise made and not kept amounts to destruction of merits earned through previous pieties. Therefore send Rāma (with him).**

### Verse 1.21.9

*krtastramakrtastram va nainam saksyanti raksasah*  
*guptam kusikaputrena jvalanenamrtam yatha*

**Перевод:**

**"Trained or not in the use of arms, as long as Rāma is protected by Viswamitra, just as nectar is protected by the flaming fire-god rakshasas will not be able to compete with him.**

### Verse 1.21.10

*esa vigrahavan dharma esa viryavatam varah*  
*esa budhya'dhiko loke tapasasca parayanam*

**Перевод:**

**“This (Viswamitra) is an embodiment of righteousness and unsurpassed among the powerful. None in this world can excel him in intellect. He is the supreme refuge in austerity.**  
**Siromani, Vasistha applauds Viswamitra’s greatness 1.21.10**

**Комментарий:**

Vasistha applauds Viswamitra’s greatness for appeasing his feigned anger. Vasistha summing up the description of Viswamitra’s prowess, says, “O Raghava, nothing, indeed, that belongs to the past and the future, is unknown to Viswamitra. He is an omniscient, exalted seer and is adorable to all. “O king, the most illustrious Viswamitra is brilliant. As he is self-reliant as noted above, you should have no reservation in entrusting Rāma with him.” Vasistha stresses Viswamitra’s arrival as a favorable one for the benefit of the king. He says, “King, Viswamitra, son of Kusika, himself is capable of resisting the demons. However, he approached you, and begged of Rāma for the goodness of your son.”

The term “putrahitarthaya” implies that the seer would initiate his whole learning to Dasaratha’s son.

Tattvadipika, Rāma's awareness about weapons 1.21.10

Parayanam means the final destination. Because, penance is an instrument used to know reality, there is the Vedic passage which reads, the brahmanas wish to know him through sacrifices, gifts and penance which never harms. The statement Rāma knows various weapons suggests all the divine weapons of the Lord came along with him at the time of his incarnation on earth. The poet says ‘arrows of various types and the bow with a long body will follow Rāma taking the shape of humans’. No one knows him is the Vedic statement. The gods do not know him even while he is with them. When it is said ‘they will not know him’, it is understood that they do not know him. Or, even when the real greatness of Rāma is described, Dasaratha did not become confident because his feeling that Rāma was his son clouded his intellect. Intending to remove king Dasaratha’s fear and also to bring good to Rāma, he is now elaborating on Viswamitra’s efficiency in protecting Rāma. The word Devadayah should be construed with the verb na vetsyanti. It means ‘even the gods do not know’.

*eso'stran vividhanvetti trailokye sacaracare*  
*nainamanyah pumanvetti na ca vetsyanti kecana*

**Перевод:**

**“This Viswamitra knows the use of various kinds of weapons which no one knows among the animate and the inanimate in the three worlds. Nor will any one even know in future.**

## Summary Sarga 21

Infuriated by Dasaratha's words, Viswamitra raged, “It is unworthy of the Ikshvakus to go back on a promise”. The earth shuddered at the sage’s anger and the devatas grew fearful! Vasishta, worshipful, wise and courageous perceived trouble and reasoned with Dasaratha, “Lord, it does not befit the most righteous in the three worlds to abandon dharma. Unjust and unworthy is this breach of promise which will augur nothing but ill. Skilled or unskilled in weaponry, Rāma, protected by Kausika, will be inviolable to the rakshasas."

“If dharma took a form, it would be known as Viswamitra! This great sage, whose might, valour and wisdom have no compare, has knowledge of every weapon that exists in the three worlds! Supreme source of ascetic power, he has the skill to wield every one of them. While Viswamitra was still a king, Lord Siva gifted those weapons to him. Not only does he possess them but has created newer ones. Never fear for Rāma's safety so long as he is with the sage. He implores you to send him not because he cannot vanquish the demons but because he wants Rāma’s fame to pervade the earth.” With all his fears allayed, Dasaratha consented to let Rāma accompany Viswamitra.

## Sarga 22

### Verse 1.22.1

*tatha vasisthe bruvati raja dasarathassutam*  
*prahrstavadano ramamajuhava salaksmanam*

**Перевод:**

**Vasistha having said thus, king Dasaratha, with cheerful countenance summoned Rāma and Lakshmana.**

### Verse 1.22.2-3

*krtasvastyayanam matra pitra dasarathena ca*  
*purodhasa vasisthena mangalairabhimantritam*  
*sa putram mrrdhnyupaghraya raja dasarathah priyam*  
*dadau kusikaputraya supritenantaratmana*

**Перевод:**

**Rāma was given farewell by his parents with recitation of mantras (for securing well-being and averting evils). Priest Vasistha sanctified him with mantras. Dasaratha kissed his son on the forehead and delivered him to the care of Viswamitra, with a heart full of cheer.**  
**Dharmakuta, Swastyayana 1.22.2-3**

**Комментарий:**

The swastyayana is a ceremony consisting of benedictions by brahmins after presentation of offerings. Aitareya Brahmana: ‘The gods said, Gayatri, get the royal soma for us’. ‘All right’, she said, ‘consecrate me with the prayers of swastyayana’. She then flew up. The gods consecrated her: ‘preti cheti cheti’. This is all ‘Preti cheti cheti. Go safe and come back safe’.

Mother’s wishes count more than others wishes. In the Mahabharata, Duryodhana, wishing victory over the Pandavas, prayed his mother Gandhari, all the eighteen days before starting for the battlefield saying, ‘Wish me well, O mother, as I proceed to fight the enemy’. She, too, said (every time) he sought her blessings, ‘Victory is where dharma is’. And did not perform the swastyayana. Vyasa explains this in the Striparva.

In Ayodhyakanda Rāma implored Kausalya to perform the swastyayana for him and she said, “May that ‘Dharma ’ protect you everywhere, O brave son of the Raghus, I give you the blessings that Vinata gave to Suparna as he prayed for nectar. Aditi performed mangala for Indra who wished to kill the sons of Diti. The same blessings I give you”.

## Summary Sarga 22

Thus persuaded by Vasishta, Dasaratha sent Rāma and Lakshmana away with Viswamitra amid Vedic chants. As the great sage set out, Vayu, the god of wind blew caressingly, the drums of heaven sounded, the skies rained flowers and the palace reverberated with the sound of conches. With a pair of quivers strapped to their shoulders armed with bows, the princes were a power to reckon with as they followed Viswamitra like the twin Aswinikumaras Skanda and Visaka.

When they reached the right bank of Sarayu, Viswamitra said, “Rāma, dear boy, sip this water. Let not this auspicious moment slip by. Here is a conglomeration of mantras called bala and atibala armed with which you shall suffer neither fever nor fatigue, nor will your beauty fade. No rakshasa can harm you even if you are off guard. Bala and atibala are the mothers of wisdom and knowledge, they will set one free from thirst and hunger. These two mantras are the granddaughters of Lord Brahma.”

With Viswamitra’s caring ministrations, Rāma and Lakshmana spent a comfortable night sleeping in the open on a bed of grass on the bank of Sarayu.

## Summary Sarga 23

At dawn the next day Viswamitra said to Rāma, “Beloved son of Kausalya, O! Rāma, wake up, it is dawn and time for oblations to the gods.” The princes rose, bathed in the waters of the Sarayu, offered oblations to the Sun-god, chanted the holy Gayatri mantra and continued their journey. Soon they arrived at the confluence of the holy rivers Sarayu and Ganga where they came upon the sacred hermitage of anchorites. The beautiful sight of the hermitage delighted the princes and aroused their interest. On enquiry Viswamitra said, “In the days of yore, this belonged to Manmatha, god of love, who at one time lived here in human form. He once dared to distract Siva who was in deep meditation. Enraged at this sacrilege, Siva let out a fearful roar, his anger blazing out of his third eye like an inferno consumed Manmatha, burning him limb by limb until he became one with space. Devoid of form he came to be known as Ananga and the beautiful place where he gave up his body came to be known as the land of Ananga. This holiest of holy place belonged to Siva and these ascetics are descendants of his disciples who live in bliss and piety”.

While Viswamitra was speaking to Rāma and Lakshmana, the holy men of that hallowed sanctuary sensed their presence and extended to them a warm welcome. In that famed hermitage the three travellers spent the night while Viswamitra regaled the princes with enchanting tales.

**Tilaka, Killing of Tataka, not a Violation of dharma. 1.24.24-31**

**Комментарий:**

Viswamitra tells Rāma that even though it may appear a sin, it is well within dharma as he would do it for the welfare of cows, brahmins and all classes of people. In addressing Rāma as the greatest among men it is implied that there is no sin in killing a woman as it ought to be done for the wellbeing of all enjoined upon a king. Whether one is wicked or not, the protector of the people has to do his duty. The duty of protection is important. This is dharma. It means the action is as per dharma. ‘Kill this woman who is opposed to dharma’. As Parasurama killed his mother at the command of his father, which does not entail any sin, when Viswamitra as a teacher who taught the science of arms commanded the act of killing, Tataka, it is not a violation of dharma. Rāma exhibits his ability to strike the target even by the track of sound.

**Перевод:**

## Summary Sarga 24

At daybreak Viswamitra along with the young Ikshvakus crossed the gushing Ganga. As the boat reached mid-stream, they heard a deafening noise and Viswamitra explained: “In the mind of Brahma was born a vision which manifested itself on mount Kailas as a lake, known as Manasa Sarovar. The river Sarayu flows from Manasa and the great noise that you hear emanates from the turbulence of its waters. The roar of the bounding flow reaches a crescendo when its waters clash with those of the Ganga”. Rāma and Lakshmana then reached the southern bank of the river where they came upon the most fearsome of forests. Trackless dense, filled with beasts and birds of prey, swarming with insects, shrill with the incessant call of crickets and the shrieking of vultures, the forest was a cacophony of multitude sounds. The wooded canopy thick and dark was made up of bilva, asvakarna, kabuka, tinduka patella and many more trees under which lions, tigers, boars and elephants roamed.

“What a forbidding forest this is!” wondered Rāma. And Viswamitra said, “Long ago this land flourished as Malada and Krusha. Here Indra tainted by the brahmahatya dosa was absolved of his sin, the impurity and taint of which cleansed by devas and rishis, was deposited at this spot. Indra became pure once again and blessed the place turning Malada and Krusha into flourishing cities of great renown”.

“Several years later a yakshini called Tataka, wife of Sunda and mother of Maricha wrought havoc in Malada and Krusha. It is here that she dwells and devours all humans. O Rāma! slay Tataka with the might of your arms and rid the forest of her diabolic presence. Thus freed from evil, the land will once again become habitable”.

## Viswamitra narrates

### Verse 1.25.1

*atha tasyaprameyasya munervacanamuttamam*  
*srutva purusasardrlah pratyuvaca subham giram*

**Перевод:**

**On hearing the excellent words of Viswamitra, a sage with unimaginable faculty, the tiger among men (Rāma) replied in a gentle voice:**  
**Dharmakuta, Sin in killing a woman 1.25.1**

**Комментарий:**

When a sudra is killed, the sinner should give in charity a one-year-old ox and eleven cows to atone for the sin. The same rule applies to one who kills a woman. In Yuddhakanda Hanumat similarly warns Indrajit who was about to kill the fake Sita.

In the Mahaprasthana of the Mahabharata, too, killing of a woman is condemned. Refusing shelter, killing a woman, depriving a brahmin of his possessions and betraying a friend are equally four deadly sins. But Viswamitra explains the reference is to the killing of a wicked woman which is justified from the angle of justice and morality.

*kathannagasahasrasya dharayatyabala balam*

Prithu replied, “O wicked one, when such killing secures the well-being of many, it’s a righteous”.

## Summary Sarga 25

Rāma asked how a yakshini like Tataka came to possess the might of a thousand elephants. The sage said, “Tataka by virtue of a boon bestowed by Prajapati on her father Sukethu, was blessed with the strength of a thousand elephants. Tataka was given in marriage to Sunda, son of Jharjha.

“To this charming couple was born a strong and invincible son named Maricha who was cursed to become a rakshasa. When Agastya killed Sunda, the enraged, Tataka with her son went on a rampage with the intent of devouring the sage. Agastya cursed

Tataka to turn into a rakshasi. Provoked and fuming, she exploded into a violent, senseless anger and resolved to render the land of Agastya unfit and unworthy of all human habitation.

“Rāma, you alone can end Tataka’s reign of terror. Diabolic by nature, maligned by the curse, she is a threat to this very earth. Kill her for the welfare of the brahmins and the cows. You need not show her either pity or compassion that is usually shown to a woman. It is the duty of a king to safeguard his subjects. Slay her, for she does not abide by dharma. Destroy her like Indra destroyed Manthara, daughter of Virochana, who wanted to annihilate the earth”.

## Sarga 26

*munervacanamaklibam srutva naravaratmajah*

**Перевод:**

**Dharmakuta, Obedience to the guru 1.26.1-6**

**Комментарий:**

This suggests that the orders of Viswamitra who is a guru, his order should be obeyed without hesitation. Dasaratha too, had instructed Rāma to do whatever Viswamitra would ask. When the order of one guru cannot be transgressed how can the orders of two gurus be defied? Therefore, Rāma agreed to kill Tataka although killing of a woman is prohibited by sastras. Rāma’s words to Kausalya in Ayodhyakanda suggest the same thing. The wise sage Kandu, killed a cow at the instance of his father although he was aware of the prohibitives of dharma. In obedience to his father, Jamadagnya Rāma cut into pieces his own mother with his axe.

### Verse 1.26.2

*piturvacananirdesatpiturvacanagauravat*  
*vacanam kausikasyeti kartavyamavisankaya*

**Перевод:**

**Tattvadipika, Killing a woman was a duty 1.26.2**

**Комментарий:**

Viswamitra asserts that killing a woman was Rāma’s duty for three reasons, First, since it was the order of his father it should be carried out. Secondly, due to respect for the father which a son should pay and, thirdly, since it is also the word of sage Viswamitra it is not a violation of dharma.

**Dharmakuta, Rāma’s action vindicated 1.26.11-12**

**Комментарий:**

Noticing that Tataka, provoked by the twang of his bow was charging towards them, Rāma said to Lakshmana, “I shall not kill her”, after having first agreed to do so out of respect for his guru’s words? A woman should not be killed instantly. First, she should be disfigured and tortured. If that is not enough, she should be killed when attacked. ‘A desperado must be killed without hesitation’ say the sastras. Thus the injunctions of the sastras should be adhered to, the accusation by people can be avoided and guru’s orders obeyed. With this intention, Rāma must have said it. Thus there is no contradiction. If Rāma did not want to kill her, he would have thrown her away with manavastra as he did in the case of Maricha. However, Rāma killed her only after he cut her hands, Lakshmana, her ears and nose while she was showering stones and mud by her supernormal power. Evening was the fast approaching which would have enhanced the strength of the demoness. Therefore, Viswamitra impelled Rāma to shake off his pity, and shoot her.

Why did they go to attend Janaka’s sacrificial ceremony uninvited? Because there is no prohibition in the sastras (Gautama).

## Summary Sarga 26

Rāma then held his bow and twanged at the string, sending out a fearful sound which echoed in all directions even as the dwellers of the forest trembled with fear. Tataka unaware and confused at what could have caused the thunderous sound ran out in a great fury.

Wrathful and ugly, she came bounding, striking terror into the hearts of the not-so-brave. Seeing her, Rāma said to Lakshmana, “She looks invincible armed with magical powers. Dismember her limbs disfigure her by cutting her nose and ears, for I am averse to killing a woman.” The infuriated monster charged forward generating a fierce dust-storm which dismayed Rāma and Lakshmana for a moment. Tataka’s rain of rocks was met with the princes’ rain of arrows, cutting off her hands as she was racing in full fury.

Deprived of her limbs, roaring with anger and writhing in pain, Tataka then lost her ears and nose to the wrath of Lakshmana. Then, when she vanished from sight but did not stop from sending another torrent of rocks, as a parting shot. Seeing Rāma and Lakshmana hit by the rocks, Viswamitra said, “This yakshini who is sinful and wicked deserves death, not mercy. She will regain her strength soon, slay her before dusk, for after sunset the rakshasas become unconquerable”. Rāma marching forward through the dust storm created by Tataka detracted the raining rocks with his arrows capable of detecting and travelling in the direction of sound.

Frustrated at her incapability to remain invisible, Tataka hurled herself at Rāma who, swift as lightning, shot her in the chest with a fatal arrow. She collapsed and seeing the mountainous heap of matter, as frightening in death as in life the gods themselves honoured Rāma. Indra wanted Viswamitra to reward him with the two weapons of Bhrisasvas endowed with ascetic power and energy. Liberated from the curse of Tataka and her dreaded presence the forest regained its radiant charm and came to look as splendid as that of Kubera’s Chitraratha.

Rāma retired for the night and woke up at dawn to the call of Viswamitra.

*madanam caiva durdharsam kandarpadayitam tatha*  
*paisacamastram dayitam mohanam nama namatah*  
*praticcha narasardrla! rajaputra! mahayasah*

**Перевод:**

**“O renowned prince, best among men, receive these astras known as darpana, soshana, santapana, vilapana, madana, the unassailable one favoured by Kamadeva and the paisacha astra known as mohana favoured by demons.**

### Verse 1.27.17-19

*tamasam narasardrla! saumanam ca mahabala*  
*samvardham caiva durdharsam mausalam ca nrpatmaja*  
*satyamastram mahabaho tatha mayadharam param*  
*ghoram tejah prabham nama paratejo'pakarsanam*  
*saumyastram sisiram nama tvasturastram sudamanam*  
*darunam ca bhagasyapi sitesu matha manavam*

**Перевод:**

**“O tiger among men! mighty prince!, accept tamasa and saumanaastras, the unassailable, samavardha weapon, mausala, satyaastra, the supreme mayadhara astra, the terrible tejaprabhaastra capable of draining the energy of the opponent, a soft weapon called sisira, supremely formidable twashtus astra, Bhaga’s terrible shiteshuastra (sharp arrowed one) and manava astra.**

### Verse 1.27.20

*etan rama! mahabaho! kamarrpan mahabalan*  
*grhana paramodaran ksiprameva nrpatmaja*

**Перевод:**

**“O Rāma! O mighty-armed prince, receive these mighty and highly exalted astras capable of assuming at once any form at will”.**  
**Amritakataka, Viswamitra invokes weapons by reciting mantras 1.27.20-21**

**Комментарий:**

Viswamitra having said in the beginning that he would give the divine weapons to Rāma, hands them with their accompanying mantras after enumeration. It is not said that he gave the weapons but that he gave the mantras. Why? Because these divine weapons were the sons of Brahma and were gods in their own right. They dwell in their own shining bodies and turn weapons only when invoked by their respective mantras. For a person to be able to use them, it is necessary to know the related mantras. Hence it is said that Viswamitra gave Rāma the collection of mantras: mantragramam dadau.

Previously, at the time of handing over the Bala and Atibala knowledge, Viswamitra had said: mantragramam grhana tvam take up these mantras but the actual handing over of mantras had not taken place. At that time only the mantras related to Bala-Atibala were given.

### Verse 1.27.21

*sthitastu pranmukho bhrtva sucirmunivarastada*  
*dadau ramaya suprito mantragramamanuttamam*

**Перевод:**

**Viswamitra, the greatest ascetic after the purification ritual stood with his face turned east and happily, conferred on Rāma a collection of the unique mantras.**

### Verse 1.27.22

*sarvasangrahanam yesam daivatairapi durlabham*  
*tanyastrani tada vipro raghavaya nyavedayat*

**Перевод:**

**The sage offered Rāma the complete collection of those weapons which even the celestials find it difficult to acquire.**

### Verse 1.27.23

*japatastu munestasya visvamitrasya dhimatah*  
*upatasthurmaharhani sarvanyastrani raghavam*

**Перевод:**

**While the sagacious ascetic Viswamitra was muttering the mystic terms of these venerable astras (addressing their respective deities), all these weapons (with their mystic power) attended on Rāma.**

### Verse 1.27.24

*rcusca muditassarve ramam pranjalayastada*  
*ime sma paramodarah kinkarastava raghava*

**Перевод:**

**The munificent presiding deities of the weapons with folded palms said to Rāma, “Here we are, at you disposal!”.**  
**Tilaka, The Weapons given by Viswamitra 1.27.24-28**

**Комментарий:**

Two maces called Modaki and Sikhari, two weapons called Asani and Aradra; Pinakam a weapon belonging to Pinaka dear to agni, Prathama and Kankala etc., weapons wielded by demons, Vaidhyadharam, jewel of a sword called Nandana out of which swords arose; Prasamana, a weapon which would put out anger of the foes, Madana that would cause infatuation in foes, Musala, a mace used by demons - all these were received by Rāma. They are called a collection of mantras because they are bound by mantras. The weapons derived their strength from the recitation of mantras. Even Bala and Atibala were conceived with the collection of mantras. The expression ‘take them’ used by Viswamitra implies that the two weapons Bala and Atibala which are useful only at the appropriate time are being given now. As far as the other weapons are concerned it was left to the discretion of Rāma in the opinion of Kataka. Actually Bala and Atibala represent only a collection oi mantras and, therefore, termed as mantragrama.

Viswamitra gave the weapons to Rāma and Lakshmana. It should be noted that both of them were taught simultaneously. ‘Japatah’ means as Rāma was repeating the mantras the deities of the weapons stood around him in a circle. The deities of all the weapons were quite were happy that they were with Rāma.

The commentator opines that although Rāma had known everything, learning through the preaching of a preceptor alone yields results. While Rāma knows the use of the collection of weapons, being not qualified to use them and being also too young to handle them, there was in him a desire to know about them. Rāma wanted to secure it, for it had been already used by the repetition of mantras.

### Verse 1.27.25

*pratigrhya ca kakutsthah samalabhya ca panina*  
*manasa me bhavisyadhvamiti tanabhyacodayat*

**Перевод:**

**Rāma received the astras he felt with his hands and commanded them saying, “Live in my mind” (serve me whenever I remember you).**

### Verse 1.27.26

*tatah pritamana ramo visvamitram mahamunim*  
*abhivadya mahateja gamanayopacakrame*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter, the cheerful Rāma bowed to the mighty ascetic Viswamitra and commenced his journey.**

### Verse 1.27

ityarse srimadramayane valmikiya adikavye balakande saptavimsassargah

Thus ends the twenty-seventh sarga of Balakanda of the holy Rāmāyaṇa, the first epic composed by sage Vālmīki.

*praticcha mama bhadram te patrabhrto'si raghava*

**Перевод:**

**“O Rāma descendant of Raghu, receive from me the effulgent weapons who are the sons of Bhrusasva and who are capable of changing forms at will. They are Satyavanta, Satyakirti, Dhrishta, Rabhasa, Pratiharatara, Paranmukha (turned back wards), Avanmukha (turned downwards), Lakshaksha, Vishama, Drudhanabha and Sunabha, Dasaksha, Satavaktra, Dasasheersha and Satodara, Padamanabha and Mahanabha, Dundunabha and Sunabhaka, Jyotisha, Krusanam, both Nairasya and Vimala, Yogandhara, Haridradaitya, Prasamana, Sarchirmali, Dhri, Mali, Vrtiimanta, also Ruchira, Pitrusaumanasa, both Vidhuta Makara, Karaveera Kara, Dhana, Dhanya, Kama Roopa, Kamaruchi, Moha, also Avarana, Jrumbhaka, Sarvanabha, also Santhana and Varuna. **Комментарий:**

O Raghava! Take these weapons starting with Satyavat and ending with Varana, the sons of Krsasva, having qualities of shining and changing forms at will. Take them, for you are worthy of receiving them for you are an incarnation of the Supreme Being who is the father of all these divine weapons.

The weapons that Viswamitra had acquired over a long period, after praying to different gods were all at once made available to Rāma without any effort. This also shows Rāma is Brahman himself because it is the sons who approach the father and the father who appoints them according to his wishes. That is why Rāma does not have to strive for them. They reach him. He accepts them happily.

## Summary Sarga 27-28

At daybreak smiling with affection, Viswamitra said, “Rāma, I am pleased and proud of the good you have done to this earth by slaying Tataka. Fulfilled and happy, I bequeath the wealth of weapons to you with love. With these you will be victorious not only against devas and rakshasas, but also against the gandharvas, nagas and uragas.”

“Starting with the celestial Danda, Dharma, Kala and Visnuchakras, Vajra astras, Brahmashivaastra, the prestigious spear of Siva, the Aishikastra and the mightiest of all, the Brahmastra; the two brilliant maces, Modaki and Shikari along with Dharmapasa and Kalapasa - all these shall be yours”.

Viswamitra taught Rāma the incantations to invoke the astra devatas to appear whenever he needed.

Imparting the means and mantras through which Rāma could withdraw the astras, Viswamitra offered him a plethora of weapons: Satyavanta, Satya Kirit, Dhrishta, Rabhasa, Pratihara, Tara, Paranmukha, Avanmukha, Lakshaksha, Vishama, Dhrudanabha, Sunabha, Dasaksha, Satavakrta, Dasashirsha, Satodara, Padmanabha, Mahanabha and many more.

## Sarga 29

## Viswamitra relates the story

\[Viswamitra relates the story of Siddhashrama. All the rishis in the hermitage worship him.\]

### Verse 1.29.1

*atha tasyaprameyasya tadvanam pariprcchatah*  
*visvamitro mahateja vyakhyatumupacakrame*

**Перевод:**

**The highly lustrous Viswamitra heard the words of Rāma of immeasurable prowess on whose query about the forest, Viswamitra explained:**

### Verse 1.29.2

*iha rama! mahabaho! visnurdevavarah prabhuh*  
*varsani subahrniha tatha yugasatani .a*  
*tapascaranayogarthamuvasa sumahatapah*

**Перевод:**

**“O mighty-armed Rāma! Lord Visnu, the foremost among the gods, and a great ascetic lived here carrying out yogic practices and penance for innumerable years constituting hundreds of yugas.**  
**Amritakataka, Yoga 1.29.2-3**

**Комментарий:**

‘O Rāma! Here in this very ashrama Visnu had performed austerities. The Virat Purusa observed austerities for the fulfilment of yoga samadhi (a state of total identification with Brahman)’, says Viswamitra. The yoga (samadhi) was in search of his own self which is the same as Brahman in His Sahaja, Bhuma, Virat and Turiya forms. When Virat with his Upadhi of samula karya becomes the Parama Karana, it is a matter of Turiya Brahma. Why is this yoga termed as viraja'? The Turiya form having unlimited knowledge and power creates himself in every epoch and creates the five actions. Viraja has adhara sakti as its principle, Samraja has kriya sakti and Svaraja has jnana sakti. The Turiya form of Brahman, which is beyond all else and which has the other three forms of Brahman (virat, etc) as its lilamurti, has all the three games (adhara, kriya and jnana). All the Vedic texts bear testimony to the fact that Virat is always performing austerities. That is why he is called Sumahatapah.

### Verse 1.29.3

*esa prrvasramo rama! vamanasya mahatmanah*  
*siddhasrama iti khyatassiddho hyatra mahatapah*

**Перевод:**

**“O Rāma! this was the hermitage of glorious Vamana. The great sage performed his ascetic practices here, hence it is known as Siddhashrama.**

### Verse 1.29.4-5

*etasminneva kale tu raja vairocanirbalih*  
*nirjitya daivataganan sendramsca samarudganan*  
*karayamasa tadrajyam trisu lokesu visrutah*

**Перевод:**

**“During the period Visnu (in the incarnation of Vamana) was observing austerities at this hermitage, king Bali, son of Virochana, having vanquished Indra and maruts and devatas ruled this kingdom and became famous in all the three worlds (for his prowess and generosity.)**

### Verse 1.29.6

*balestu yajamanasya devassagnipurogamah*  
*samagamya svayam caiva visnumrcurihasrame*

**Перевод:**

**“While Bali was performing the sacrifice (to confirm his position as Lord of the three worlds), the devas got together with agni in the forefront and approached Lord Visnu at this hermitage, saying:**

### Verse 1.29.7

*balirvairocanirvisno yajate yajnamuttamam*  
*asamapte kratau tasmin svakaryamabhipadyatam*

**Перевод:**

**‘O Visnu! son of Virochana is performing a great sacrifice. Before its completion, our purpose ought to be achieved.**  
**Amritakataka, Categories of gods 1.29.7**

**Комментарий:**

While Bali was performing a sacrifice a question arises as to how an asura could perform a sacrifice? What kind of sacrifice it is? To whom is it offered? Madhava Yogin infers that both the devas and asuras perform yajnas in order to achieve the eternal proximity with the Supreme Being according to their own thinking. As to the questions, who were the gods that the asuras addressed their sacrifice, the commentator observed that there are two categories of gods.

Karmadevas are those who achieve godhood by their good deeds and once their merits have exhausted they fall from godhood. These are the gods who the asuras fight. Ajanajadevas are those without beginning or end. They are eternal truth and a part of the Brahman. They are connected with yajna. It is the Karmadevas who are afraid of other mortals or asuras achieving godhood by performing sacrifices. So they usually try to put obstacles in the path of the sacrifice.

Tilaka, Gods propitiated 1.29.7

It has been established in Uttaramimamsa (Vedanta) that the gods are in the form of images and that there are two kinds of gods viz. Karmadevas and Ajanadevas. Those who attained godliness by means of karma are called Karmadevas. The Ajanadevas being constantly engaged in reciting mantras precede Karmadevas. And, therefore, realized the meanings of the sacrificial mantras ahead of Karmadevas. Although Karmadevas are hostile to Ajanadevas it is not a mistake to propitiate the Ajanadevas in sacrifices. In fact, karmadevas bring obstacles. Yet they give the right to perform sacrifices.

Tilaka, Incarnation of Visnu as Vamana 1.29.7-12

Goddess Aditi and goddess Saraswati propitiated Lord Visnu in order to get him as a son just as Kasyapa penanced for one thousand divine years for the same purpose. If the Lord is different from His penance will not the Advaita or non-duality be contradicted? There is no contradiction of non-duality because the Lord himself is called the manifestation of penance (tapomurthi). ‘Tapas’ is derived from the root, ‘tap’ which means, ‘to reflect upon’.

'Tapatmaka', therefore, means those who have not performed penance cannot visualize Him who is the embodiment of knowledge.

*etamasramamayanti raksasa vighnakarinah*

### Verse 1.29.27

*yatharham cakrire prjam visvamitraya dhimate*

## Summary Sarga 29

Emerging from the forest, Viswamitra narrated to the brothers the history of Siddhashrama that was on their way. “Visnu as a pious ascetic had once lived here immersed in yogic practices and penance for many hundred yugas. This holy hermitage formerly belonged to Vamana, an incarnation of Lord Narayana who had also attained perfection here. From then on, this place where Kasyapa lived was known as Siddhashrama.

“When Visnu was observing austerities here, emperor Bali, son of Virochana, had vanquished Indra, the Maruts and devas. Renowned for his boundless generosity, Bali had established his sovereignty throughout the three worlds. While he was performing a yajna to retain that supremacy the gods led by Agni assembled here in this hermitage and told Visnu of Bali’s yajna. ‘Transform yourself into a vamana, a dwarf and accomplish the mission,’ they said and the mission was to defeat Bali’s attempt at supremacy through his generosity.

“While the devatas were pleading with Visnu, Kasyapa arrived effulgent like the fire, his brilliance enhanced by virtue of his association with Aditi. Kasyapa, having ended his rigorous penance of over a thousand divine years, said, “O Lord! I beg you to grant a boon to my wife Aditi, to the devas and to me. May you reincarnate as our son! May you be born a brother to Indra for the deliverance of the tormented devatas, and third, may this hermitage be renowned as Siddhashrama.”

“Thus the Lord in response to Kasyapa’s prayer incarnated through Aditi as Vamana, the dwarf and set out to the land of Bali. Visnu ever the giver and never the receiver in the Vamana form desired of Bali three feet of land. It was granted. The two feet measured by the feet of the Lord took up the entire surface of the earth and the dome of the sky. The Lord needed yet another foot, and where would he put it? And Bali bowed his head. Lord Vamana put his third foot on his head. Bali sank. Visnu then returned all the three worlds into Indra’s care”.

“In this hermitage which removes the fatigue of worldly life, which once belonged to Vamana I now inhabit by virtue of my deep devotion to the Lord. The notorious demons are still a danger to my yajna. You have to slay these wicked rakshasas right here and now. Let us go to that sacred hermitage which is as much yours as it is mine.”

Assured by Rāma and Lakshmana, sage Viswamitra commenced preparations for the yajna with a serene mind.

## Summary Sarga 30-31

The valiant princes Rāma and Lakshmana now stood ready to avert the marauding demons from disrupting the sacrifice. Pleased at their assurance to repel the rakshasas, the sages requested the brothers to stand guard for six nights until the conclusion of the yajna.

Bowing to the ascetics, the famed Ikshvaku princes watched over the hermitage for six days and nights forgoing sleep to protect Viswamitra. On the sixth day Rāma warned Lakshmana to be on guard and doubly vigilant as they waited impatiently for the demons. Just then the sacrificial fires tended by Viswamitra suddenly leaped into a great blaze enhancing the radiance of the altar. The Kusa grass, ladles, vessels and flowers showed up starkly in the brightness of those flames. A thunderous noise was heard and out came Maricha and Subahu, pouring down torrents of blood. Furious at the desecration of the holy altar, Rāma called out to Lakshmana, “Watch as I scatter these evil, flesh-eating rakshasas, like wind-blown clouds, with the weapon, Manava The weapon hurled Maricha into the ocean, a hundred yojanas away, where he lay crushed and unconscious. Rāma then turned his attention to the other blood-thirsty rakshasas who were a menace to the yajnas.

Rāma then shot the fierce agneyastra and shot at Subahu who, pierced to the heart, fell down dead while the rest succumbed to vayavyastra. Viswamitra achieved his purpose and Rāma had honoured his father’s word.

With Viswamitra’s mission accomplished, Rāma and Lakshmana were happy. Yet their mission was not complete. Something awaited them. Viswamitra told them that Janaka, king of Mithila, was going to perform a yajna and that he had the wonderful bow of Siva with immeasurable powers, obtained from the gods by Devaratha, Janaka’s ancestor. The gods, gandharvas, asuras and even kings have failed to string it. Could Rāma and Lakshmana give it a try? Viswamitra too would accompany them. The princes were willing. With the setting of the Sun the travellers camped on the banks of the river Sona. Rāma, enchanted by the lush green groves asked Viswamitra about the history of the place.

## Sarga 32

## Description of the four sons of Brahma

\[Description of the four sons of Brahma and the dynasty of Kusanabha - enraged Wind-god turns the daughters of Kusanabha into humped-back ones.\]

### Verse 1.32.1

*brahmayonirmahanasitkuso nama mahatapah*  
*aklistavratadharmajnah sajjanapratiprjakah*

**Перевод:**

**“There was a great ascetic named Kusa, born to Brahma, an ascetic indefatigable in vows, knowledgeable in dharma and a respecter of the virtuous.**  
**Dharmakuta, Religious duties of sons staying in joint and separate families: 1.32**

**Комментарий:**

Kusamba and his brothers pursued their religious activities independently. Marichi observes “If the eldest in a joint family performs a religious rite the benefit goes to them all”. This is confirmed by Manu and by Kṛṣṇa in “Aswamedhikaparva” of the Mahabharata.

Narada also says, “There is a common religious duty for all the brothers living in an undivided family but when there is separation the religious duties must also be separately performed”. Gautama also agrees: “After separation, religious activities increase”.

Thus, when the brothers live separately their pursuing religious activities independently is justified but in this case when the father is alive, how can the sons act independently as they do not have the right to do so? Since Manu says, “One obtains this world by devotion to mother, the middle region by devotion to father and the Brahmaloka by devotion to one’s guru. To treat them with respect is like performing a religious rite. He who does not respect them, however, performs all other acts of piety in vain. So long the are alive, no religious performance is necessary unless, of course, they permit you to do one. Their service is the highest religion in its true form, the highest penance. Anything else is only a subordinate dharma”.

Sons’ Right to Father’s Property:

Manu declares, “The ancestral property goes to all the sons equally after the death of the parents. While they are alive, they cannot claim it. Only three are without property, a wife, a slave and a son. Whatever they earn belongs to those to whomsoever they belong”. Therefore, it makes sense that the four sons of Kusha

performed religious duties independently. Rāma, too, gave portions of the kingdom to his and his brothers’ sons as is clearly stated in the Uttarakanda. This kind of division (and distribution) is not possible, however, in case of irreligious sons. Manu says, "The brothers engaged in activities inadmissible by dharma have no right to the wealth".

Yajnavalkya and Bodhayana agree that a girl after maturity (menstruation) should wait for her father’s orders for marriage.

### Verse 1.32.2

*sa mahatma kulinayam yuktayam sugunolbanan*  
*vaidarbhyam janayamasa caturassadrsan sutan*  
*kusambam kusanabham ca adhrrtarajasam vasum*

**Перевод:**

**“That great soul, Kusa, married the princess of Vidarbha born in a noble family and a match for him. He begot four virtuous sons who resembled him. They were Kusamba, Kusanabha, Adhurtarajas and Vasu.**

### Verse 1.32.3

*diptiyuktan mahotsahan ksatradharmacikirsaya*  
*tanuvaca kusah putran dharmisthan satyavadinah*

**Перевод:**

**“Kusa addressed his four brilliant sons who were highly enthusiastic, pious, truthful and were wedded to duties of the warrior race:**

### Verse 1.32.4-5

*kriyatam palanam putrah dharmam prapsyatha puskalam*  
*rsestu vacanam srutva catvaro lokasammatah*  
*nivesam cakrire sarve puranam nrvarastada*

**Перевод:**

**‘O my sons, govern with righteousness so that you will acquire immense merit’. Hearing the words of the rishi, the four sons who were the best among men and revered in the world constructed four cities as their abodes.’**

### Verse 1.32.6

*kusambastu mahatejah kausambimakarotpurim*  
*kusanabhastu dharmatma puram cakre mahodayam*

**Перевод:**

*tassarvagunasampanna rrpayauvanasamyutah*

**Tilaka, The Episode of Kusanabha’s Daughters and the Wind-god 1.32.15-21**

**Комментарий:**

To entice the daughters of Kusanabha the Wind-god makes overtures of love. To the girls such a request is improper and immoral. 'We can remove you from your godhood. We do not curse you because we want to preserve our power of penance'. They threaten they plead, 'Being under the control of our father we are not independent in the choice of our husband'. The king admires their tolerance and their self-restraint.

‘Brahmatapas’, means meditation on Brahman with single-minded attention or a devoted study of the Vedas.

The commentator gives a detailed account of the event from the Vamanapurana. Karsikasamhita, Sankarasamhita, and own book 'Gangamahatmyaprakasa'.

*aham vah kamaye sarva bharya mama bhavisyatha*

*calam hi yauvanam nityam manusesu visesatah*  
*aksayyam yauvanam praptah amaryasca bhavisyatha*

### Verse 1.32.18

*tasya tadvacanam srutva vayoraklistakarmanah*  
*apahasya tato vakyam kanyasatamathabravit*

**Перевод:**

**“At the words of the untiringly blowing Wind-god the hundred maidens laughed and said:**

*antascarasi bhrtanam sarvesam tvam surottama!*  
*prabhavajnah sma te sarvah kimasmanavamanyase*

**Перевод:**

**‘O best among devatas! you move within all living beings, we feel your impact. Why do you insult us?**

### Verse 1.32.20

**Перевод:**

*mabhrtsa kalo durmedhah pitaram satyavadinam*

**Перевод:**

*tasam tadvacanam srutva vayu: paramakopanah*

**Перевод:**

**Перевод:**

*ityarse srimadramayane valmikiya adikavye balakande dvatrimsassargah*

Thus ends the thirty-second sarga of Balakanda of the holy Rāmāyaṇa, the first epic composed by sage Vālmīki.

## Summary Sarga 32

Viswamitra explained: “Kusa, born of Brahma was a great ascetic who was married to the princess of Vidarbha. She delivered four sons: Kusumba, Kusanabha, Adhurtrajasa and Vasu. Kusumba founded the city of Kausambi, Kusanabha the city of Mahodaya Adhurtarajasa created Dharmaranya and Vasu built the city of Girivraja. This land belongs to Vasu, and is known as Vasumathi. Five majestic mountains surround it where flows the river Sona. Born in Maghada this beautiful river meanders from east to west through rich farmland turning it into golden rows of green fields.

‘To Kusanabha the royal seer and his queen Ghritachi were born one hundred worthy daughters who were like streaks of lightning in a thunderstorm and like stars among clouds. They sparkled, danced and sang with great joy and greater abandon. One day Vayu, the wind-god chanced upon them. Charmed by their beauty he said “I desire all of you to be my wives. Forget the world of mortals and attain immortality. Youth is momentary and more so in humans. Marry me and be ever youthful”.

“In disdain the young girls answered “O Vayu, supreme among the gods, you pervade all life and we are aware of your powers. Why do you disgrace us so? We are the daughters of Kusanabha and he is our master. A god you may be, but we can topple you from your lofty heights. Do not dishonor our father, he may prove to be your death. It is our duty and dharma to many those chosen by him”. Enraged, Vayu pervaded into their bodies, twisting, disfiguring their limbs and turning them into ugly hunch-backs. Saddened and shamed, the damsels in distress told their father about what had happened”.

Thus ends the thirty-third sarga of Balakanda of the holy Rāmāyaṇa, the first epic composed by sage Vālmīki.

## Summary Sarga 33

Kusanabha listened to his daughters, commended their courage and unparalleled patience: “Your tolerance in the face of such an intimidating situation is truly laudable. Patience is charity. Patience is virtue. Patience is truth. Patience is fame. Patience is dharma. The world is founded on patience”.

King Kusanabha sought the advice of his ministers about the marriage of his daughters. They told him of a Maharshi by name Chuli who was at one time immersed in great penance. “Serving and looking after his needs was a gandharva called Somada, daughter of Urmila. Pleased with her ministrations, he asked what boon she wanted and wished for a son endowed with ascetic power. And the son she begot was known as Brahmadatta who now lives in the city of Kampilya”.

“King Kusanabha made up his mind to give his daughters in marriage to Brahmadatta. During the wedding Brahmadatta ceremoniously received each one of the princesses by taking their hand. The very touch of his hand transformed the maidens; their disfigurement and anguish vanished as they regained their radiance and beauty. Delighted, Kusanabha sent Brahmadatta on his journey with due honours back to his kingdom with his wives.”

*ityarse srimadramayane valmikiya adikavye balakande catustrimsassargah*

Thus ends the thirty-fourth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Rāmāyaṇa, the first epic composed by sage Vālmīki.

## Summary Sarga 34

Viswamitra continued: “After Brahmadatta returned to his kingdom Kusanabha performed Putreshti for a son. Kusa, son of Brahma, told him that he would beget a son called Gadhi who would bring him everlasting fame. That Gadhi was my father born of the Kusa dynasty. Hence I am known as Kausika. Satyavati, my sister, true to her name was an upholder of dharma and ever diligent in performing austerities. She was given in marriage to Ruchika. Divine and beautiful she flows in the Himalayas as river Kausiki for the benefit of mankind, for their pleasure and prosperity”.

Viswamitra further told Rāma that he lived in the vicinity of those mighty mountain ranges for the love of his sister alone and if it were not for the yajna he would not have parted with her to go to Siddhashrama. While the narration went on, dusk had gently nudged out the light of day and the first half of the night too had passed. Trees were motionless, birds in their nests and beasts in their lairs slumbered in the dark that pervaded every comer of the forest. The sky put forth its heavenly show of a myriad stars shining like so many twinkling eyes while the cool-rayed Moon, created joy in the hearts of all living creatures. The roaming hordes of owls along with the flesh-eating yakshas and rakshasas moved stealthily in the eerie stillness of the night.

Journey of the fire-worshippers (Agnihotris):

The words 'after offering oblations to fire' etc. indicate that people vowed to the worship of fire must carry with them the Fire-god. Trikandamandana supports this view.

The Mahabharata writes: “During pilgrimage a person should perform the three sandhyas (routine worship). He should not go to a holy place without taking a bath, in an unclean condition, after taking food or in the period of impurity caused by a childbirth or death in the family”.

**Tilaka, Ganga - Tripathaga 1.35.14**

**Комментарий:**

The gods scared of demon Taraka request Himavan to offer Ganga to Siva for a son who could save the three worlds. Himavan offers her in conformity with the dharma on condition she could freely choose her path. Ganga chooses the path of wind (Pranava) on her own. Uma the second daughter of Himavan conducts intense penance for the grace of Siva and wins Him. The gods request Uma to bear the energy of Siva. But Brahma says Uma is not capable. Humiliated, she protests she can. May you take the form of water, Brahma curse. And she remains in a boiling vessel. The vessel breaks spreading water on the feet of Visnu in the sky. Under stress she falls down from the edge of the feet of Visnu and becomes famous as Visnupadi. The Vamanapurana says Ganga remains in the pan on the top of Brahmanda. The Kamikasamhita has it that Ganga water falls along with external water (Brahmajala) of the Brahmanda. Brahma holds the external water in his waterpot with which he washes the feet of Narayana. And keeps it back.

Sankarasamhita gives another version. Gauri once closes Siva’s eyes with her palms. And then Siva’s third eye on the forehead shines. The palms of Gauri begin to sweat out of fear and the sweat flows down. Brahma collects it in his water-pot.

On Bhagiratha’s appeal Brahma grants him the most sacred water in the form of Brahman.

Viswamitra tells Rāma ‘I will explain how Ganga became tripathagamini, the river that flows in three courses. First she went the way of the sky. Then she ascended to heaven. As she flowed on the earth, she became the remover of all sins’. Ganga is Tripathaga, flowing in three courses on earth, heaven and patala or the underworld. The story of Ganga is also depicted in Vamanapurana.

## Summary Sarga 35

As the dark night gave way to a bright dawn, Viswamitra who had spent the night on the river Sona along with the entourage of sages and princes forded the river. They walked on and on, feasting their eyes on beautiful woods and forests through which they traversed.

Many miles later, they came upon that great river Ganga, revered and loved by the sages. The breathtaking beauty of the bubbling flow enhanced by majestic swans and soaring cranes. The august assembly halted on the bank surveying the sylvan splendour with great delight. Bathing in the holy waters they lighted their sacrificial fires and offered oblations to gods and ancestors.

On enquiry Viswamitra related the story of Ganga: “The Lord of the Himalayas was blessed with two daughters of unsurpassed loveliness, Ganga and Uma. Uma was given in marriage to Mahadeva, Lord of Kailas. Their mother Manorama was the daughter of mount Meru”.

## The devatas create obstacles

\[The devatas create obstacles to the marital bliss of Maheswara and Parvati - goddess Parvati curses the devatas and the mother earth.\]

**Перевод:**

### Verse 1.36.8

*tato devassamudvignah pitamahapurogamah*  
*yadihotpadyate bhrtam kastatpratisahisyate*

**Перевод:**

**“Then the devatas led by Brahma were exceedingly alarmed. ‘Who will be able to bear the power of the offspring if it is born here and now’, they reflected.**  
**Amritakataka, Story of Uma 1.36.8-28**

**Комментарий:**

The gods try hard to stop Rudra from releasing his seed after one hundred and seven years of love-making. But when the gods wanted that Uma should give birth to Siva’s son, why did they strive to stop Siva from releasing his seed? Because they were scared that when Uma gives birth to a son after the gestation period he will be so powerful that nobody will be able to tolerate his might and radiance, much less to see him since they had already seen the blinding blaze of Virabhadra born of the sweat of Rudra. So they decided that the son of Siva and Uma should not be born.

So they went to Siva for he alone was able to control the unthinkable power that would be released. Having no other safe haven, they fell at Siva’s feet and said "We bow to you. The world will not be able to support your semen, as it would be equal in brilliance to innumerable Virabhadras. The very thought paralyses our minds”.

Then what should be done? The gods advise Siva to perform the Brahma tapas along with Uma. What is the use of the Brahma tapas and why should Siva perform it? Because he might be able to secure his seed. In the beginning of conception we have an embryo. The semen remains over all parts of the body and soul. “Hold your mercurial semen within the sahaja eight-fold yoga" said the gods. But then the question arises about the effect of holding the semen through sahaja yoga in the body? The answer is it will save the world. It is said that the semen, of the Brahman is held within the Aditya mandala (in the constellation of the Sun) and it saves the worlds. If it is released, like Siva’s semen the worlds will be destroyed. Hence ‘Na alokam kartumarhasi’. So Siva accepted their plea. All the gods are his limbs and if the limbs are destroyed and he will become a branchless trunk (Sthanu). So, he said “All right! I shall hold my seed and so shall Uma. The gods and earth can be happy now. Uma will hold her seed in the fire”. It is said in the Vedas that the menstrual flow in the women is a form of agni. Siva will hold his seed in water. If their seed falls on the earth, it will burn the entire world and even the gods. “Therefore, to protect them, we shall hold our seed.” But stirred by long love the semen will drop from its place. It is in the form of moisture and infallible and the best one capable of giving birth to a son who will be able to fulfil gods’ requirement. Who will be able to hold it? Saying this Siva released his seed with which the entire earth along with all its mountains and forests became filled.

In order to protect the seed, the gods appointed agni. One of the reasons is that agni is said to be the Lord of the earth (Prthivya adhipatih). Further, he was holding the seed of Uma. So agni was advised to enter the semen of Rudra along with Vayu. That tejas (glow) became like a white mountain and later by the effect of that place became a thicket of reeds which was divine and which looked like agni and Aditya. That tejas was born as Kartikeya.

Due to agni holding it for some time and then releasing it, the gods become very happy because Rudra had withheld the original seed in order to protect the world and released the dried up seed for the cause of the gods. The gods and seers then worshipped Uma and Siva. But Uma did not accept their veneration. “Since you have deprived me of bearing a son by Siva, you shall not beget sons from your wives. You did not want me to give birth to my husband’s son, like other people but instead did the injustice that the gods wanted you to do. Therefore, you will be the wife of many and still never give birth to a legitimate son.”

Siva was unable to take back the curse nor could he see the gods so crestfallen. So he prepared to leave for the west to perform the austerities. He went west of the Himalayas and on the northern side of the mountain on a peak performed penance with Uma. Viswamitra told Rāma the story of Uma in detail.

Tilaka, Story of Uma 1.36.8-27

If Lord Siva bears his energy in his own self, of what use is it to the world? The scriptures say ‘what is in man in the form of semen is the form of energy in the Sun. That form of energy is light which is the disc of the Sun itself. In that circle the whole world is being protected, if the reverse happens, there will be a calamity (Viparyaye Viparyaya).’ If the sun perishes the whole world will collapse.

Siva says, ‘I along with Uma, will bear the fire of my energy in my own self’. So he bears the semen. It will turn into fire (blood) in women. Since this world cannot withstand the extraordinary energy, if released, there would be devastation. This is the sense.

The gods said, ‘This earth will bear it because it has unlimited power of forbearance’. This is the implied sense. The gods engaged agni to receive the energy released on the earth as he is the Lord and well-wisher of the earth. The wind which accompanied him helped him move. That energy acquired the form of the white mountain and having entered the earth by means of agni, was moving (as he carried it). Then that energy got the form of a thicket of needles like the fire of the Sun at the place of its entry as a result of its greatness. Since agni carried the energy for some time, it should be noted, Karttikeya originated from agni. There was joy among the gods that Siva’s energy was borne for the benefit of the world and that the energy that fell transformed into Kartikeya for the sake of the gods. But there was anger in Uma, for Siva did not accept Uma engaged in his worship. She cursed the Earth, saying ‘Be not in one form. May you give fruits for a variety of seeds in the same field. Be wife to many husbands (Lords of the earth or kings).

The implication is, ‘If only she (earth) had not conceded to bear the energy of Siva, Uma would have received it. She would have had that son’.

## Summary Sarga 36

“Many years ago”, continued Viswamitra, “the greatest of ascetics, Siva married Parvati and they spent one hundred years in marital bliss. Yet Parvati did not conceive. Perplexed, Brahma and the gods wondered who could bear the baby born of this divine union. They then invoked Lord Siva and pleaded with him to retain his energies of creation within his most magnificent self. Siva declared that he could have done so, but since the energy was already dislodged, he asked them who could bear it. And the devatas replied that the earth would.

“The energies thus released spread over forests and mountains, which were lit up with an unearthly brilliance. The devatas implored Agni and Vayu to pervade into the divine energy transforming it into the Sveta mountain. On this grew a forest of white reeds and from this radiance was born the most glorious Karttikeya.

“Uma was furious. She cursed them all for preventing her from begetting a son: ‘Just as I stand deprived, may your consorts too be sterile! ’ Nor did she spare the earth, whom she bitterly blamed and cursed. ‘May you be the wife of many masters! May you never experience a mother’s love!’

“Siva travelled to the northern slope of the Himalayas where along with Parvati he entered into a great penance”. Concluding his narration, Viswamitra asked Rāma and Lakshmana to listen to the origin of Ganga”.
