Thus it is only inappropriate to attribute to Rama (who had deserted Sita for fear of scandal) the fault of killing Vali who had illicit relationship with a woman other than his wife, out of desire to obtain Sita back.

While the deceit by Yudhistira who was covetous of kingdom, results in sin, Rama’s infamy incurred due to the killing of Vali with the purpose of safeguarding a higher virtue in the form of keeping one’s promise does not result in any sin.

4.9.14-15

Kamandaka says, ‘The elephant thumping on the mountain would break only its tusk. For those who attempt the impossibility the result would be trouble. Except distress no other fruit results. The rebuttals of action are agonizing. Discretion attended by preeminent knowledge is the abode of wealth.

4.11.4

It may be understood that it was necessary to visit all the four oceans for rituals as described by Tara to Ravana in the Uttarakanda of the Ramayana.

4.11.35-36

In Dronaparva Bhurisrava says, ‘Noble men will not strike the intoxicated, the frightened, one without a chariot, one who is beseeching and one who is overtaken by calamity.’

Arjuna in Dronaparva gave assurance to kill Jayadratha, if not, he would reach those worlds of patricide on matricide.

**4.11.67**

**The power of Vali is even superior to Vayu because one has not seen the entire leaves of the trees falling even when the wind blows fast. Vali is ‘ativyathana’, that is he can make a tree lose all the leaves and is capable of shooting arrows unlike other monkeys.**

Saptabhumimvivesa 4.12.3-4

‘Saptabhumimvivesa’ means though the arrow was shot to pierce through one sala tree, the arrow cleft seven sala trees and pierced through the land of the ‘asrama’ and entered into the ‘rasatala’ the lowest world going through the seven worlds. Having gone down to ‘rasatala' the arrows killed the demons in the ‘rasatala’ and reached back Rama.

Vali emerges like the sun 4.12.16-25

The commentator says that Vali emerged like the Sun from the western mountain. The statement isjustified from the point of view of those that live on the northern side of mount Meru-The mountain behind which the Sun sets is the mountain behind which it rises for those on the opposite side. So the emergence of the Sun from Astagiris justified.

Rama’s confusion 4.12.32-33

It is improper to say that Rama got confused between Sugriva and Vali when he can never err. Moreover when Sugriva ran back to Rsyamuka, Rama could have identified Sugriva. While Rama could have killed Vali whose life span was over. Rama had to act as a human being in order to please Sugriva imposing disillusionment on him. It, therefore, suggests that there is no confusion because the Lord appeared as though he is confused but not in reality. When the condition was such it is incorrect to say that Rama uttered a lie.

Saptajanah 4.13-18

On their way to Kjshkinda Sugriva along with Rama and Lalcshmana walked by a forest where seven sages lived and penanced fora hundred years sustaining on air before attaining heaven. These sages called Saptajanah obtained godhood with their austerities.

Sugriva is compared with the Sun 4.14.9

Tî the commentator what Valmiki said appears impossible because the Sun cannot be seen surrounded by stars. Here the word ‘Suróṁ’ means the ‘Moon’- He justifies it bó giving the derivation of the word ‘Surya’ according to grammar, The second explanation given by him is that this sloka is an example of adbhutopama, a figure of speech in which something impossible is imagined by the poet and presented as explanation. The word viparita is said to have the meaning of ‘night’. Surya means the full ‘Moon’) so the statement means ‘you shine like the full ‘Moon’ surrounded by stars at night”.

Nakshatramalaya 4.14.10

‘Nakshatramalaya’ means, ‘like the Sun surrounded by the garland of stars. This is a figure of speech ‘ upamalikopama'. There is also ‘atisayokti’ as the Sun is described as wearing a garland of white flowers when it is still dawn. The commentator says that some interpret the word as ‘viparita’ the seventh case. The Moon on the full Moon day is called Surya, and Viparita means night.

4.14.18-19

In Gadaaparva Bhima says, ‘0 son of Gandhari! be a man. Being composed, fight. You will not live today in spite of Indra being your refuge. Sanjaya to Dhrutarashtra — “Your son, a tiger in war, provoked again and again by the god of speech, did not tolerate the speech like the best horse, the whip.’

Vali’s appearance 4.15.1-6

Vali whose complexion was reddish yellow like twilight and who was bright like the evening sunlight became dull very soon like the eclipsed Sun overpowered by his own spite. This simile predicts the imminent catastrophe. Vali appeared like a pond from which lotuses were removed by elephants. His fangs were compared to the lotus stalks and he was compared to the blazing fire to indicate the change of his complexion due to excess of rage.

4.15.27

Daksa says, the accrual of fruit of the gift made to father is hundred fold, to mother, a thousand-fold, to sister a hundred thousand and to brother imperishable likewise with regard to violence.

4.15.30

Visnupurana : ‘A wise man should not breed antagonism against the superior or the inferior.’

Killing of Vali was not a deceitful act 4.16.27-32

When Sugriva was losing strength, Rama made his intention clear to kill Vali. It is, therefore, proper to kill Vali keeping Sugriva in front. Killing of Vali on the grounds of transgression of dharma apart, killing in disguise by a righteous person (dharmika) like Rama is but improper as it is prohibited. As Manu says — ‘One must not kill (a warrior) standing on the ground, a eunuch, with folded hands, frightened and engaged with another (in a battle)’.

Gautama too says, ‘Injury is not a crime in war except against a person (warrior) without horse, charioteer, weapon, with folded hands, turned away with dishevelled hair, seated on the ground / tree, an envoy, a cow, a brahmana etc.’

So also in Dronaparva, when engaged in war against Satyaki, Bhurisravas addressing Arjuna who chopped off the latter’s arm deceitfully says, ‘knowing the ethics of war you have struck me, one who was not waging war against you. Noble men never strike at a person who is drunk, mad, frightened without a chariot, who is soliciting and who is in adversity. Being a friend of Krishna you must not inflict such pain’.

However it should not be said that Vali’s killing was not done deceitfully.

Vali’s indirect praise of Rama 4.1.13-43

Starting from ‘tam drstva raghavam’(Sloka 13) up to the end of this. Sarga, the slokas have another meaning. Even though Vali was intent on saying harsh words to Sri Rama, his speech was actually in praise îf Rama according to the commentator.

Vali spoke the words, which were harsh outwardly, yet they were full of dharma and had no arrogance in reality. Sloka 15 means, “Rama, you have obtained indescribable glory on account of killing one who was indulging in sensuous pleasures. I obtained death from you while I was engaged in combat and that way also I obtained glory. It has been stated in the scriptures that a king who does not punish the guilty invites sin upon himself. Since you have punished me now, you obtained merit in the form of avoiding the sin. It has also been said in the scriptures that those who are guilty become free from all blemishes when they receive the punishment from the kings and that they enter heaven like meritorious persons. So I have also obtained the quality of sinless men on account of the punishment given by you.”

Vali\`s reply to Rama as to why he came to get killed knowing Rama’s friendship with Sugriva was that death caused by Rama would bring him liberation and so it is highly superior to the death caused by Sugriva.

Slokas 14-18: A thought occurred to Vali that Rama does not kill some one who is engaged in combat with another, Rama struck him when he was fight Sugriva. Why?

Sloka 1 9-20: “I do not th ink you are a condemned ora pseudo — righteous soul. I know you are neither unrighteous nor sinful. I do not think you are a charlatan. But I do know that you are the lord endowed with virtues like sinlessness.”

Sloka 22: “You have been born in the family of kshatriyas for maintaining order in this world. You are most compassionate and so it is impossible that you commit any unjust act.”

Sloka 25: “O Rama! is it a fact that you are born in the family of kshatriyas and kn own as follower of dharma? but you are in fact a doer of cruel acts masquerading as a do-gooder? "This is incompatible in you.”

“Even ordinary kings do not act according to their sweet will, what to say about a great Lord like you?

Why should you have concern for dharma? There is no need, because the rules of dharma apply only to human beings. You are divine. Your mind is not fixed in wealth because you are the lord of Lakshmi.

Sloêṁ 43 Samagatahshould be understood as Samṁ agatah ‘I reached him as a faithful servant’.

Sloka 44: Here it is to be understood that Rama came near Vali only to bless him by showing his lotus feet.

In this sarga the commentator tries to show that Vali’s words which apparently condemn Rama actually praise him. For this purpose the commentator converts statements into questions, supposes some questions, splits' some phrases and interprets some words in an unusual manner. The commentator’s interpretations, however, are not convincing.

Vali questions Rama’s propriety in killing him 4.17.14-17

Killing of an animal without reason is improper. ‘Living beings must not be injured’ is the scriptural injunction. Never should one desire to kill a creature is the statement of Manu. Here is no reason. Is it due to enmity? Was Vali a source *of trouble? Had he done any offence? Was the killing perpetrated for any use of its flesh, skin or any other thing? Was it because there is no sin in killing? Was it for the task of tracing Sita?*

Not the first one, because enmity is not established in the absence of any wrong committed by Yali. Not the second one, because by the examination of lexicons the word kantaka means an insignificant enemy among many meanings. When Vali is not even an enemy he being an insignificant enemy is ruled out. Neither is it the third. The sinful act which could be the cause of killing is itself not proved here as the thefts of gold etc., which are sinful acts are not found in Vali. Not the fourth one. As laid down by Manu, ‘amongst five-nailed animals, only iguana, alligator, porcupine, rhinoceros, tortoise and hare are to be eaten’. But the flesh of a monkey is forbidden food. Therefore, as flesh it is not used.

Like the use of the hair of animals like goats, camels and bones in fine cloth or like the use of the claws of tiger and the tusk of elephant etc. in the adornments of swings, damsels etc. or like the use of the skin of a cow, a buffalo etc. in foot-wear, the use of claws, bone, hair of a monkey is never seen in the world. Nor in the Vedic rites. Only the skin and horn of an antelope or the skin of a boar, a bull etc., the wool, the hair (of a bull), the quill etc, are useful in rubbing sacred threads, the seat etc.

Or as enjoined in the Vedic rites the use of the vessel of rhinoceros, buffaloes etc., in the offerings to the deceased, the use of hair, skin etc, of the monkey is never seen. Not the fifth one. In killing a monkey the expiatory rite is ordained because of the accrual of sin is certain.

As Manu says - ‘Having killed a swan, a crane, a peacock, a monkey, a hawk and a cock one should gift a cow to a brahmin’. Here, sparsana means dana gift. Not even the sixth. Since it was possible to procure Sit a through solicitation of Vali there was no need to kill Vali on that account.

Vali questions Rama’s desire 4.17.31-54

Both Rama and Vali have different desires. Vali is an animal living on forest food Rama is a human who eats cooked rice, While Vali is a monkey, Rama is a lord of men. This sarga is devoted to the prayer of Vali. It is not acceptable to Vali himself as he declares later saying that whatever words he has spoken are out of ignorance. He tells him not to find fault with his questions. Valmiki did not intend to present Vali as a monkey with bad expressions.

Rama’s reasons for killing Vali 4.18.6-32

Killing is justified because it is the duty of kings to kill animals in hunting, and because accepting the wife of a brother is a transgression. However, it is no justification, for the reason that Sugriva had also done the same thing. And it is no killing in hunting. Yet Vali has transgressed dharma being in Rama’s kingdom. And the offender of dharma needs to be punished by the king.

In Rajadharma, ‘the duty (dharma) of a king is not to tolerate or excuse a person, however dear, committing a sin either in act or speech.

In Manava dharma too it is said— ‘An unrighteous and unlawful person must be subdued with effort in three ways - by confinement, by punishment and by various kinds of killing’. ‘A king who forgives or bears with a person indulging in crime will soon perish or will be an object of hatred to the people’.

The king and the person concerned are purified though killing. Otherwise, both will earn sin, as in the story of Sankha and Likhita in Rajadharma. There were two brothers of commendable austerity who lived in separate beautiful dwellings. Once in the absence of his elder brother Sankha, Likhita entered his hermitage, collected the ripe fruits and ate them. When Likhita was eating, Sankha returned to the hermitage and told his brother in a rage. ‘You have committed a theft. Therefore, go to the king and report your act. Likhita went to the king Sudyumna and told thus, ‘Oh, king! unpermitted by my elder brother, I ate his fruits. I may be chastised. Then the king cut off the two hands of Likhita. Thus punished, he went back to Sankha and sought his forgiveness. Sankha replied T am neither angry nor have you wronged me but you have transgressed dharma for which you have atoned. Now take a dip in the river Bahuda and propitiate pitrs (Manes). Thus urged, Likhita having taken a dip got back both his hands. Surprised, he approached his brother and showed his hands. Sankha told him, T did it by my power of penance’. Then Likhita asked why he did not exhibit the (same) power and purified him before. Sankha said T acted like this because I am not the king to punish you. Thus the king and your self together with the pitrs are purified’. In this way, the king with his act obtained the highest good.

Because this Vali has committed sin (adharma) in the form of seducing the wife of his brother he has been punished. According to Apastamba Sutra — ‘When character droops, the guilty must be punished with the removal of genitals with testicles. When a youth, well-dressed enters unknowingly a place where other married women, maidens are found he must be punished; and Narada says, A person who seduces his mother, mother’s sister, mother-in-law, maternal uncle’s wife, father’s sister, paternal uncle’s wife, a student’s wife, sister, her friend, daughter-in-law, daughter, a teacher’s wife, a woman of the same lineage with common ancestral name, one who has sought refuge, a queen, a female ascetic, nurse, a pious woman, a woman of higher caste and a woman not of equal status is to be inflicted with punishment not other than that of cutting off his genitals by the king.

Therefore, for his redemption Yali’s killing is justified.

It should not, however, be argued that the transgression of dharma in the form of approaching a brother’s wife applies to Sugriva also A second husband is ordained for women in five adverse circumstances — when the (former) husband has disappeared or dead, when he has become a eunuch or is fallen’. Hence, after the death of Vali, Sugriva’s acceptance of Tara is not wrong. The circumstances are not the same. Though non-injury is dharma, ‘For kings, fulfilling a vow is the uppermost of all dharmas'. Likewise in the Mahaprasthanikaparva of the Mahabharatam, ‘returning a refuge, killing a woman, stealing the property of a Brahmin and breach of friendship (treachery to a friend) are considered equal to the desertion of a devotee’. Yudhistira says to Sakra, although the desertion of a devotee is greatly sinful to kshatriyas, keeping the vow is the highest dharma.

In Adiparva the Pandavas state that there is no fault in killing an animal: ‘The act of killing the enemies is but equal to the killing of animals for kings. Killing of animals guilelessly or guilefully is admitted. This is the dharma of the kings.’

Because a transgressor of dharma deserves punishment, a vow must necessarily be kept up and there is no sin in killing an animal, killing is proper. Further, Vali must be killed because he is the enemy of Rama’s friend, Sugriva and because he is also the friend of Rama’s enemy, Ravana.

In Dronaparva, Krishna declares that he is the friend of Arjuna by killing the enemy of Arjuna. I shall, for the sake of Arjuna, kill them all including Kama, Suyodhana, horses and elephant. Further, a friend’s enmity is one’s enemy. Krishna says in Udyogaparva, ‘Know that I am one with the Pandavas who follow dharma. One who hates them will hate me and one who follows them will follow me’.

Therefore the enemy of a friend is one’s own enemy and hence killing him is but proper after all. And also, in order to protect a person who has become one’s own friend killing of his enemy through unjust means is not a blemish. Only because of this that Arjuna cut off the arm with the sword of Bhurisravas who was about to kill his pupil Satyaki in extreme distress. But to Bhurisravas’s objection that when he was engaged in a battle with another, cutting off his arm is sinful, Arjuna replied (to Bhurisravas) that to protect his man at the time of calamity killing of the enemy by unlawful means is necessary. Otherwise it becomes a sin, thus posited in Dronaparva, ‘I know the ethics of wars as I am well-versed in all sastras. I will never commit any sinful thing. If I see Satyaki killed in the war then I will incur sin for my lapse’.

Therefore, the killing of Vali in disguise in order to protect his ally Sugriva who is about to be killed by Vali is not improper.

Yet though Vali’s killing is acceptable yet doing so by placing Sugriva in front is not. Rama could have killed Vali himself. However, when mutual quarrel ensued between the two brothers, one who sought his help should get it.

Rama’s reply to Vali on dharma 4.18.15-16

Subtle dharma has to be known from those who radiate with the learning acquired from noble preceptors and not to be known by those who are otherwise, ‘hridisthah’ implies that he is the dweller in the heart as the soul-principle, which is all-pervasive. He knows the good and bad of all beings signifying ‘I know your sin though you are an all- pervading Lord. You have been consulting the monkeys who have no training from the preceptors. How can you know dharma? How can you protect the people who should be protected? You have therefore fallen from the dharma and deserve punishment.

Vali’s adultery 4.18.19

The commentator raises a question, ‘Is not Sugriva to blame because he made the wife of his elder brother his queen which is clear from the stanza uttered by Angada when he performs fast unto death vide 4.55.3. He says ‘Sugriva is to blame because he made his elder brother’s wife his queen and has clandestinely married my mother.’

But Rama clarifies, ‘You are a sinner because you have married Ruma who should have been treated as your daughter -in-law while your younger brother is alive. Sugriva was not aware that you were alive and he made your wife his queen and hereafter (after your death) he will make her his queen. Moreover, even among the three classes of men the brother-in-law marries his sister-in-law if the brother dies without having children. When such is the case, Rama contends, the monkeys, as animals, should pay penalty of death for adultery. This indicates that to accept other women who have lost their husband is a practice among women of classes other than the first three. Such a practice can be seen among sudras. The question is, ‘how can the rules of prohibition prevailing among men be applied to the lower beings?’ One can see that the system of the rule of the kingdom by a king is seen among the lower beings since they are also endowed with knowledge like human beings. Therefore, their sin visits on them also. They also offer libations like Sampati to Jatayu.

Moreover, Indra who was authorized for the practice of dharma had to face the sin of killing a brahmin when he killed Vrtra.

It is stated in Purvamimamsa that the gods are forbidden from offering sacrifices for themselves except Indra. However, regardless of religious acts the gods are also entitled to giving gifts and also acquisition of gifts and of spiritual knowledge according to Uttaramimamsa. Similarly lower beings who are also enlightened are to do the same. Moreover, in all the worlds, which signify all the gods, there is a reference to the Lord also and therefore gods are entitled for all. That is how the sacrifices of Candra and Varuna are remembered in the Puranas.

Moreover, there is entitlement for the three classes who are equipped with Vedic knowledge. Therefore it is the intention of sages like Vyasa and Valmiki and the Lord himself that they are gods and are also entitled. Jaimini appears to be ignorant of this matter. When Markandeya enquired Jaimini about dharma in order to get clarification (from Jaimini) he got the dharma taught through a bird, which knew the truth and which lived in the woods of Vindhya. Now ‘the birds are not entitled to knowledge’, it is for this reason that Rama performs the last rites of the king of eagles. Later on offering of water by Sampati, the brother of Jatayu, to the Lord is also not irrelevant.

Rama’s comments on Sugriva living with Tara 4.18.22-26

Even though seduction of a wife is common to both Vali and Sugriva there was a fundamental difference between the two offenders. Rama points out that Sugriva lived with Tara, the wife î Vali, only after deciding that Vali has been Kelled by Mayavi. In contrast Valigrabbed Rama, Sugriva’s wife even when he knew that Sugriva was alive. “One who violates the chastity of one’s own sister or of brother’s wife should be punished with death”.

Rama’s justification in killing Vali 4.18.25-34

Rama killed Vali on the authority of Bharata. Is it not a false statement? No, it is a resolution of Rama himself and Bharata endorsed it. There is no mistake if it is understood that Bharata s order is an established fact as far as punishment of those who are guilty is concerned. Moreover when Bharata has ordered the protection of the innocent in his empire such an order has to be carried out. The other reason for killing Vali is to restore the lost wife to Sugriva and to fulfill the promise made by Rama to make Sugriva king. Each of these reasons is enough to kill Vali. Therefore, the rule followed is according to scriptures.Think it over, says Rama. ‘You are worthy of punishment because you have kidnapped your own younger brother’s wife. I have also to discharge my commitment to Sugriva. If I did not kill you I would be violating the duty of a Kshatriya since I have heard about your adharma. It is therefore, my dharma to kill you.’

‘As an avatar, I have to punish the offenders and so I have followed dharma.’ The suggested meaning is, it is dharma to help one’s friend and Rama has followed dharma in killing Vali. The purport is ‘while you are repenting for the evil act done you are following dharma.

If, on the other hand one says T am a sinner and I may be punished, the king convicts or aquits him and that person gets relieved of his sin. If the king does not punish, he becomes the sinner.’ ‘Therefore to punish you is our duty’ says Rama.

Rama’s justification for killing Vali 4.18.27-45

Ramajustifies his killing of Vali on fourgrounds, namely abduction of brother’s wife, Rama’s duty to implement Bharata’s orders, friendship with and promise to, Sugriva. “When others commit blunder kings vigilantly punish them with death or incarceration for purification. By that punishment sin is absolved. Kings are not independent in their judgment on this as they are bound by the rules of sastras” according to Rama.

Rama says that he has no regrets about hiding and killing Vali because it is common for kings to kill animals from hiding places using nets and traps and it is wrong on the part of Vali to censure Rama because kings are embodied gods.

The commentator quotes the words of Manu which mean that people who have committed blunders become purified by undergoing the punishments meted out by kings and thereby become fit to go to heaven.

Killing of Vali is in conformity with dharma 4.19.11-12

As in Apadharma, ‘In times of calamity one may feign to be blind or deaf; one may use the bow made of grass; one may be down in the recumbent posture of a deer. The enemies subjugated may be killed by means of conciliation (sama) and other expedients. One may deceive like a wolf. Just as a branch of tree with fruits is made to bend and then felled. One must carry the enemy on one’s shoulder till the turn of time. When time changes he must be smashed like a pot on the stone. One should kill the enemy, through expedient means of conciliation (sama) and bribery (dana). One should also appease him by dissension (bheda) and force (danda)'.

In fact, the killing of Vali is in conformity with *dharma.* For, Rama had made friendship with Sugriva in the presence of fire.

4.19.15

‘Tebhyo nah Sumahad bhayam'. The purport is, ‘when Sugriva arrives here along with Rama and Angada who is consecrated as heir-apparent it is impossible for Tara to stay there. A conflict might arise with the vanaras of Sugriva and others who were cheated by Vali. Some maintain that it is ‘Tara who says, we do not appreciate your stay here.’

4.20.11

It is suggested that seizure of others’ wives reduces one’s longevity, causes enmity of kinsmen and destruction of life and wealth. Manu states, any other thing in the three worlds will not lessen a man’s life than approaching another man’s wife. Indulging in improper act, enmity with kinsmen, challenging the strong, and faith in womenfolk are the four doors to death. Disrespect to the elders, disregard for women and hostility to a brother are acts of condemnation.

Karma phala 4.21.2

Here by the adjective means a living being will reap the fruit of pleasure and pain conforming to the act either good or bad performed under the influence of the respective impression of dharma and adharma accumulated through beginning- less worldly life (samsara).

So also Apastamba states: ‘The performance of stipulated duties for all castes yields bound less superior happiness. Having discharged them (in the transmigratory world) with the remnant fruit of karma (action), one gets one’s caste, beauty, colour, strength, intelligence, retentive power, material wealth and abidance in dharma. Like a wheel (cakravat-takravatuvat) one experiences pleasure (lives in pleasure) in both worlds. Just as abundance of fruit of the seed of plants and trees depends on the excellence of soil, the abundance of fruit of the bad deed is indicated.

Even in Moksadharma, ‘The embodied soul (Atma) tainted by evil turns his mind on the evil path. Having done bad deed sets in greater suffering. The sinful and wretched suffer distress due to distress only, suffering due to suffering, fear due to fear only, death due to death only. On the other hand, those who are righteous devoted restrained and prosperous more upwards, upper regions and become happier’.

Grief after death 4.21.3

Vidura says in Striparva ‘Living beings (creatures) obtain pain or pleasure by their own deeds. Death need not cause any grief. It is as natural as plunging in and emerging out of water.

4.22.1

It is described here that Vali looked around before his life ceased. So it appears that Vali was still alive. Despite this fact Hanuman said in the last sarga that Vali’s obsequies bad to be arranged, it is not a wrong statement because Vali bad been hit by Rama’s arrow, which never fails and thus Hanuman knew that his death was certain.

Vali’s successor 4.22.5

When the king dies the son should get the kingship and not the younger brother. Since the son is too young to rule the kingdom and is dependent on Sugriva he should not see his ruin. Even Rama cannot rule the kingdom of Kishkinda. Therefore Sugriva should rule the kingdom and Angada become heir-apparent. It should be noted that since Angada is heir apparent, he should become king after Sugriva and not Sugriva’s sons.

4.22.6

Since Vali is invincible he casts off his frame after an arrow of Rama fatally strikes him. Others opine that even the death that Vali had in the hands of Rama also adds to his reputation.

Duty of a prince 4.22.19-23

Nitisara avers: A son must always be devoted to the service of his father through body, mind and speech. And whatever is repugnant to the father must be repugnant to the son also.

4.24.8

In Karnaparva, ‘Krishna says to Arjuna, ‘On account of killing the eldest you would indeed go to hell?

4.24.20

Krishna says to Rukmini, — ‘One without a son will not attain higher worlds. Barenness is better than begetting a bad son. A bad son is hell while a good son is heaven. A person desirous of a son should want such a son who is learned, compassionate, modest and righteous.

4.24.36-37

Sruti ordains, ‘A wife is half of her husband’s body.

Adiparva too says, A wife is half of a man and is his best friend’.

Tara’s lamentation 4.24.39-41

Tara says ‘If you kill me, it will not be adharma although you have committed the sin of separating husband and wife’ Or, ‘ Sita who has been abducted from you recently will not stay with you for long as a result of my curse’.

Mrtyu (death) and Kala (time) 4.25.4

Bhisma tells Yudhistira, in Anusasanaparva, the story of Gautami and her son bitten by a snake to death. When a hunter seeks Gautami’s permission to kill the snake, she says no. For life is controlled by Karma. Neither death nor time nor serpent but Karma is responsible. In Rajadharma Vyasa says Kala rules life. No one other than his own karma is the cause of his own destruction. Karma is the cause of mortality. All are under the sway of Karma.

Supremacy of time 4.25.5-7

The supremacy of time in all actions is discussed here. It is said that ‘all activities in the world are bound by actions done in the past. One cannot be a master of time’. The commentator quotes Suta Samhita.

‘Na kalasya bandhutvam asti’ implies that time does not favour any one. ‘Nahetu’ means either in its beginning or in its end. In other words, you cannot either destroy or remove time. Lord Rama is neither subordinate nor under any one’s control. A wise man should accept happiness or misery which is the result of what he had done. The purport is ‘one should neither be sad nor delighted nor blame one’s own abilities. Similarly, dharma etc also comes under the control of time’.

4.26.12-13

In Adiparva Dhrtarashtra placed Yudhistira as heir apparent.

4.26.14

Because of contamination caused by muddy water etc., kings take up expeditions in autumn not during rainy season: Raghuvansam.

4.26.34-40

Bhishmaparva praises the propriety of the Pandavas,

4.27.35

The word ‘ Kriyapara’ suggests that Rama had the quality of making proper effort that would lead to success. ‘Daivaparayana’ means Rama had the fortune on his side, ‘Astika’ indicates that his belief was the cause for his qualities. ‘Vyavasayi' means that Rama always took proper actions.

4.23.1-53

"The poet remembers the vedic statement, 'The rays with which the Sun scorches are used by Parjanya to shower water'.

4.28.3

Taittariya, Harivamsa, etc. say the sun draws water and releases it in monsoon.

In Vanaparva, it is said that the Sun saluting the Northward direction takes hold of the saps through Sun rays and descends the earth. Even Kalidasa says the Sun receives water in order to release it thousand told.

4.28.10

Manu: ‘The brahmacaris may wear skin of black deer, of Ruru (a kind of deer), of goat, of hempen, silk and of sheep in succession’

Gautama: ‘The garments made of black antelope, of Ruru, of goat are worn by celibates.

In regard to wearing sacred thread, Manu: ‘The sacred thread woven threefold upwards made of cotton for a brahmin, made of hempen for a king (Kshatriya) and made of wool for a merchant (Vaisya)’. Khadira Grhysutra: ‘One becomes invested with sacred thread raising the right arm and letting the thread of Kusa grass over the neck’.

Manu: The girdle of a brahmin is made of Munja grass woven threefold, of a Kshatriya, the bow-string; of a Vaisya, the thread of Kusa’.

Gautama refers to ‘girdles of Munja, bowstring, hempen and cotton fibre (Sutra).’

Regarding holding of staff Manu says, ‘by scriptural injunction the staff of a brahmana is made of bilva (aegle marmelos) and patasa (a kind of teak — butea frondoza), of a Kshatriya, vata (banyan-cypraea moneta) and Khadira (acacia catechu), of Vaisya, Pippala (fig-ticus religiosa) and udumbara (fig-ricus glomerata)'.

Manu and Gautama prescribe the height of the staff. The staff of a brahmana is up to the height of his hair (on the head), of a Kshatriya, up to the forehead and of a Vaisya, up to the nose. These should be straight, without cicatrix i.e. scarless, pleasing to the eyes, not disturbing the mind, with bark and unscathed by fire.

4.28.11-24

The Visnupurana, describes the wonderfulness of the rainy season.

Rainy season, the time of sleep of Hari 4.28.25

Lord Visnu goes to sleep during Caturmasya, i.e. from 12thday of the bright half of Asarh to the 12thday of the bright half of Kartika: Varahapurana, Padmapurana, Brahmavaivarta, Hemadri, Bharata Bhavisyam, Harivamsa.

In Hemadri and Bhavisya the ways of taking the vow are described. One must worship Visnu (Cakrin) with Jasmine garland with this mantra (hymn) - ‘oh, Lord of the universe! with your sleep the world sleeps, with your wakefulness the world wakes up. Acyuta! Be pleased. In this way having worshipped the idol of Visnu with folded hands in front of Visnu, one should submit — ‘I will take up this observance lasting for four months of rainy season (yearly) till the awakening of the Lord, Oh, Acyuta! Make it bereft of obstacles’.

Even in Harivamsa, ‘The celestials make lord Visnu (Garudadhavaja) who had been blissfully sleeping awake.

See movement of cranes in rainy season in Meghadutam and Pratapamartanda

*Recitation and chanting of* Vedas *4.28.36-37*

Taittiriya and Manavadharmasastra prohibit music. Then why Lava and Kusa sing in the Ramayana which is a dharmasastra? Music, however, is permitted in Grihasthasrama. But Lava and Kusa were Brahmacharis.

But Vedic singing is prescribed as part of Vedic rite. Apastamba and Aswalayana permit music. Yajnavalkya says music is the medium of moksha. It leads the singer to Brahmattwa, Sabda Brahman reaches Param Brahma. It is part of Brahmopasana.

The seven songs (gitikas) viz., Aparantaka, Ullapya, Mudraka, Prakari, Avenaka, Govinda and Antara and four gitikas Viz., Raggatha, Panika, Daksavihita and Brahmagitika lead to moksa. One attains Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha through music, through lute and flute: Sangita Ratnakara.

Sage Valmiki has delineated the story of Rama in the form of a song (Gita) with the intention of meditating upon the Supreme lord.

*Season prescribed for study of* Vedas *4.28.54*

Brahma means Veda. The brahmanas recite Samaveda during the month of Bhadrapada or Prosthapada. The specific time of the month is mentioned in Khadiragrhya Sutra. Manu, Gautama, Asvalayana, Apastamba, Bodhayana, Kaladarsa, Kurmapurana enjoin upon brahmacharis to study the Vedas in Sravana / Bhadrapada.

4.28.61-64

‘Those discarding their own interest bent upon doing what is beneficial to others are great men, those without leaving their self-interest all the same inclined to do good to others are ordinary men, those for their self-interest impede what is good to others are demons in human form, but we do not know who are those who destroy what is good to others are demons in human form, but we do not know who are those destroy what is good to others without any reason.’

4.29.7-9

With the eyes clouded by passion a person (king) even while seeing cannot see (is blind).

Acquisition of friends 4.29.9-10

Here by the phrase 'mitrasamgraha', ‘acquisition of friends’ does not mean new friends but guarding the acquired friendship. Kamandaka: ‘Acquisition of friends is of three kinds — approaching from afar, distinct speech pleasing to the heart and gift preceded by honorific speech’.

Kingdom 4.29.11

Kosa (treasury), danda (punishment) and allies are only cumulative causes for a kingdom, and by saying ‘Sarvari' — ‘all’ the unsaid ministers and others are also meant, without which the glory of great kingdom (maharajya) is not obtained.

Kamandaka: ‘A kingdom comprises seven limbs that are mutually complementary; if deficient even by one limb it cannot be in a good condition’. The king cannot attain Trivarga (three-fold human values - Dharma, Artha and Kama).

Manu speaks of those seven limbs of the state, ‘Master (king), minister, city, kingdom (country), treasure, military power (rod as a symbol of authority and punishment) and allies’.

4.29.12-15

Kamandaka: ‘After the decision its execution must not exceed the stipulated *time.*

Friendship 4.29.16-26

As in Kamandaka: ‘Giving help to a genuine, non fraudulent friend, embracing him when he visits home, giving gift to him to the best of one’s capacity and showing tolerance is one who knows time and place to act for others’ benefit’. Rajadharma: ‘A king must not err in giving protection to the allies.’

4.30.1

Harivamsa: Lord Sakra milched the divine milk-yielding cows which ooze out the fresh, pure milk held by the cluster of clouds.’

Lakshmana’s exhortations at Rama 4.30.16-20

‘Kim atmuapaurusya parabhavena', what is the use of self-defeating? The time for meditation has begun says Kataka. He contends that the syntactical arrangement will otherwise suffer if any other reading is accepted. What is pointed is, ‘until you get the benefit engage yourself in actions which arise out of reflections’. ‘Svakarmahetum ca kurusva’, means keep doing the rituals such as worshipping gods. Every object that is not fire is burnt. Therefore the Sita who is carried away was only her image, the real Sita is in fire, which you have propitiated’.

4.30.29-31

Kalidasa: Struck by the ichor-scented flowers of plantain trees, the elephants as if out of envy exuded ichor sevenfold.

4.30.38

Kalidasa in the context of describing autumn, ‘High humped bulls wild with excitement battering down the banks of rivers imitated his prowess with playful ease.’

4.30.39-54

Like the sluggish stride due to laziness of a wanton woman enjoyed by many lovers, the slow flow due to thinness of autumnal rivers is beautiful.

‘A gem whetted on a touchstone, a victorious warrior wounded by weapons, an elephant weakened by the flow of ichor, a river with dried sand banks in autumn, the moon with the residual digit, a young woman fatigued by amorous dalliance and the kings who have given away their wealth - (all these) shine by thinness.’

Tara’s living with Sugriva justified 4.31.1

‘It is not an offence on the part of Tara to have accepted another man’s hand because the Sastras have sanctioned the acceptance of another man by a woman on the grounds of husband’s death etc.

Manu says, ‘when a husband has disappeared, is dead, has renounced or a eunuch or fallen — in these calamitous situations another husband is ordained for a woman.’ Anusasanika: In the death of a husband a woman may court husband’s brother (brother — in — law) as husband’.

Narada: ‘Though married, a woman may be given to another bridegroom if the first husband is found to be of different caste, fallen, eunuch, one who has committed an unlawful act, of the same patronymic family, a slave or diseased for long’.

‘These five are forbidden in Kaliyuga — remarriage of a married woman, taking eldest brother’s share, killing of a cow, marrying the wife of a brother and a vessel for water (used by ascetics).

Sugriva accepts Tara only after Vali’s death was confirmed. But Vali accepts Rama while Sugriva was still living.

4.31.6

Anusasanika: ‘Those who desire the highest good here and hereafter are the composed men who have shunned anger’.

Kamandaka: People treat the king who gets angry without reason like a snake’.

4.31.8

As Yidura says in Udyogaparva ‘Pleasing words lead to auspiciousness while foul speech engenders trouble’. Kamandaka: One should make the world one’s own by amicable speech. Like a sword falling again and again harsh speech cuts asunder the vital part of the heart. It flares up the powerful. The flared are always hated.

‘An intelligent man does not hit in the heart. Both weapons and words, rude and rough, when discharged, cut asunder the vitals of the embodied souls.

Transgression of Tara and Sugriva 4.31.21-22

Manu: By being unfaithful to the husband she suffers calumny in this world; else, she takes birth in the womb of a jackal and is troubled by sinful diseases’.

‘After her husband’s death the chaste woman guarding her celibacy goes to heaven even without a son like the celibates. By this demeanour of a woman restrained in mind, speech and body she obtains the highest fame here and the highest worlds elsewhere’.

Therefore, Tara’s approach to a man other than her husband is wrong. Similarly, it is improper on the part of Sugriva to cohabit with Tara. Cohabitation is prohibited with another’s wife before or after marriage?

Visnupurana: ‘Infatuation with other’s wife causes fear in men in both worlds. Being dead the person attains hell and even in this world his longevity decreases’.

Apastamba: ‘These seven (re-) married girls (punarbhuh/Paunarbham) who ruin the family must be shunned — one who is bestowed by words, by mind, who has completed the ceremony with the marriage thread prior to marriage (Krtakautukamangata), who has touched water, who has held hands, who has circumambulated the fire and a (remarried) widow begetting children.’

Bodhayana: - ‘There are seven kinds of the remarriage — given through words, through mind, given over, who has circumambulated the fire, who has taken seven strides, has been enjoyed and one who has a married husband — by marrying her a man does not earn merit’.

Yajnavalkya: condemns remarriage of a punarbham by these words — ‘whether or not a woman has sexual contact with a man remarried is considered to be punarbhu (who is sanctified by the rites again).

Narada: ‘one who is not blemished by sex before marriage is a virgin. She is the first kind of a remarried woman and she deserves to be purified again by the sacred rites’. Tara being elder brother’s wife approaching her amounts to the sin of violating Guru’s (the wife of Guru) bed.

Samvarta: By going to the wife of a paternal uncle or a brother’s wife one should perform a penance laid down for going to the wife of a Guru. There is no other expiation than this.’

Manu: ‘The sin of approaching a woman who is not to be approached has to be averted by these expiatory acts, the expiatory act of approaching a Guru’s wife is recommended for a person who cohabits with other women, friend’s wife, son’s wife, Virgins and Candalis, sister / daughter of a paternal aunt, daughter of one’s aunt and mother and the daughter of one’s brother. Having approached them the person must perform Candrayana vrta. A wise man must not approach these women for courtship.’

Apastamba: ‘Approaching female friends of one’s mother / elderly women and likewise the female friends of the father / elderly man or other married women, a person falls.’

Narada: ‘A person who approaches a mother, mother’s sister, mother-in-law, maternal uncle’s wife, father’s sister, paternal uncle’s wife, a student’s wife, sister, her friend, daughter-in-law, daughter, a teacher’s wife, a woman of same lineage (with the common ancestral name), one who has sought refuge, a queen, a female ascetic, nurse, a pious woman, a woman of higher caste, and a woman not of equal caste / status is said to commit incest or becomes a violator of teacher’s bed’.

4.32.20

In Vanaparva, Draupadi states ‘A person who has helped formerly may have committed a grave sin but by remembering his previous help, his mistake has to be condoned’.

Anger on a women 4.33.36-39

Rajadharma: ‘Anger must always be controlled in respect of gods, kings and brahmanas in particular and the aged, women and the deceased’. Vidura in Udyogaparva too says, ‘O, Dhrtarashtra! those who are brave in respect of brahmanas, women, cows and ascetics fall like ripe fruit from the stalk. Brahmanas, cows, relatives, children, women and those who have given food and those who have taken shelter should not be killed’.

The Mahabharata: ‘Pious men who want rewarding future do not see the forehead of another woman like the digit of Moon on the 4thday’.

4.33.49

Vanaparva: ‘The guilt resorted to out of ignorance must be pardoned.

4.34.10-11

Even the animals and goblins will not eat the dead-bodies of the ungrateful’.

Rama’s invincibility 4.35.17-18

Ravana has also a comparable army and the entire army under the control of Sugriva cannot be killed. But Tirtha makes a syntactical arrangement stating that with the help of Sugriva alone the demons including Ravana cannot be killed. Further he maintains, ‘Vali indeed said that it was futile to request Sugriva to kill Ravana’. But the whole interpretation is meaningless because Rama’s request to Sugriva for help becomes unacceptable, as his strength is invincible.

King’s duties 4.38.22-23

Rajadharma: ’Increasing the number of friends, subduing enemies and worshipping the pious are the king’s duties’. Vidura Udyogaparva: ‘wise men call him dull-witted who befriends an enemy, hates and kills a friend and embarks upon an evil action’.

Manu: ‘The afflicted must not cause affliction.

Udyogaparva: ‘Therefore a person who delights in dharma must always eschew speech that is injurious and harsh’.

Numerals 4.38.30

Numerals begin with one and ends in Parardha \[100,000,000,000,000,000\], Taittiriya Sruti — Eka, Dasa, Sata, Sahasra, Ayuta, Prayuta, Nyarbuda, Samudra, Madhya, Anta and Parardha. In Lilavati and Siddhantasiromani too, ‘Eka is (1), Dasa 10, Sata 100, Sahasra 1000, Ayuta 10,000, Laksa One lakh, Prayuta Ten lakhs, Koti One crore, Arbuda Ten crores, Abda or Abja Hundred crore, Kharva, Nikharva, Mahapadma, Sankhu (Sanku), Nidhi (Jaladhi), Anta (Antya), Madhya and Parardha 100,000,000,000,000,000. These numerals are fixed by ancestors for transaction’.

4.38.32-34

The words starting from Sata and ending with Parardha are numerals.

Ten thousand = Ayuta

One hundred thousand = lac

One hundred lac = One koti ( crore)

One crore lac = Sanku

One thousand Sankus = Arbuda

Ten Arbudas = Madhya

Ten Madhyas = Anta

Twenty Antas = One Samudra

Twenty Samudras = One Prardha

4.39.11-12

The numbers used to represent are Eka, Dasa, Sata, Sahasra, Ayuta, Laksha, Prayuta, Koti, Arbuda, Vrnda, Kharva, Nikharva, Mahasaroja, Shanku, Samudra, Madhya, Parardha etc. Each succeeding number is ten times more than the preceding number.

The Vindhyan range and the several rivers mentioned here are not in the south of Kishkinda. The inconsistency is irreconcilable.

The geographical description is not at all factual. That ‘Vanga’ etc., are shown in southern direction from Kishkinda passes strange to our ears.

Some interpolator in north (Kurukshetra as the central region) might have committed several anachronous inconsistencies betraying his ignorance of geography.

Sugriva's instruction to the troop assigned to eastern region 4.40.12-63

Sugriva orders Vinata and his troop to go and search in the eastern direction and search all areas including the Ganga. But Ganga is not to the east of Mount Meru. The interpretation is, it is the area east of Aryavrata i.e. land between the Himalayas and the Vindhya.

The word Sudarsana dvipa (slokas 61 -63) refers to Jambudvipa because it has the shape of Sudarsana. Sugriva asks the monkeys to search the caves and valleys of that mountain in whose brightness the eye of all living beings shines. The eastern direction is called Purva’ because it was made the first door of Sunrise. It is said Sugriva does not know the areas beyond, as there is no Sun there.

Mandehas 4.40.16-42

Taittiriya Sruti - ‘The demons performed severe penance. Prajapati blessed them with a boon. They will fight against Aditya. Thus the demons have been fighting with the Sun till it sets. After some time, with the water consecrated by the hymn of Gayatri they become quiet. When the Brahmavadis (the expounders of Veda) turning towards East in the twilight throw water sanctified by Gayatri upwards, the waters becoming Vajra (thunderbolt) throw those demons into the island of Mandeharuna.

4.40.42

Kataka believes that the two verses: 4.40.41 and 42 are spurious. He thinks that there is no reference to ‘arunadvipa’ on to which according to the scriptures, the Mandeha demons are thrown after they are killed by the brahmins with their firepower. Kataka also points out that the fort area has to be located after finding out the sea of ghee and curds, which lies between the seas of spirit and milk (Ksiroda).

Significance of four quarters 4.40.50-64

Purva is the first quarter because the Sun is seen first there or because of the association with the island formed before. Udyogaparva : ‘Because the gods in ancient times occupied this direction first it is called Purva. Vivasvan gave the Guru Kasyapa a gift with Sruva (ladle). Therefore, the direction is called Daksina. Since after the day the Sun withdraws its rays, this direction is called Pascima. The direction that redeems man from sin is called Uttara.

Visibility of the Sun from mountain peaks 4.40.59-60

‘Drsyo bhavati bhuyistham’. The commentator observes that the Sun goes round Jambudvipa northwards after he sets there. Then he appears clearly to those who live in Jambudvipa after reaching the high peak of mount Saumanasa. This phenomenon refers to Satyayuga. In Tretayuga he appears on the milky ocean. In Dvaparayuga he appears on Suroda and in Kaliyuga in the middle of Lanka because he will be visible at Jambudvipa to men.

4.40.65-71; 4.41.1

Visnupurana describes the world of Yama as full of terrible hells: Raurava, Rodha, Sukara, Taptakumbha, Taptaloha, Mahajvala, Lavana, Vimoha, Krimisha, Lalabaksha, Vedaka, Visasana, Adohmukha, Puyavaha, Rudhiranbas, Vaitarani, Krsna, Asipatravana, Vahmijvala, Sandamasayatana, and Svabarjana.

One who gives false witness goes to Raurava, one who kills foetus, Guru, cow and strangles a man goes to Rodha; a drunkard, a murderer of brahmin goes to Sukara, a stealer of gold goes to Taptakumbha. A killer of kshatriya / vaisya, he who approaches the wife of a spiritual teacher (Guru), who has incest with a sister or kills an ambassador, a seller of liquor, a galore, lion seller and a deserter of an adherent falls into the Taptaloha. He who commits incest with his daughter or his daughter-in-law, shows disrespect to elders falls into Mahajvala. He who uses false language falls into Lavana. One who derides the Vedas or sells them, and who approaches a woman not to be approached, a transgressor, who hates his father, brahmanas and gods and who spoils precious gems, falls into Vimoha hell. One who does evil goes to krmisa hell wherein worms are served as food. He who takes food before offering it to the guests, manes and gods falls into the terrible hell called Lalabhaksa. One who makes arrows falls into Vedhaka hell; one who makes lances, swords etc., falls into Visasana hell. A foreteller, one who is impetuous a seller of lac, flesh, liquor, sesame or salt will go to the same hell; one who fondles cats, cocks, goats, dogs, wolves and birds reaches the same hell also. A theatre performer, a fisherman, son of an adulterine, a poisoner, a spy, a paramour of an unchaste woman (one who lives by the prostitution of his wife), one who approaches one’s wife on full and new moon days, a charcoal burner, a treacherous friend, a soothsayer, one who performs crude rites and one who sells soma creeper — all these go to the hell called Rudhiranbhas. One who destroys villages goes to Vaitarani hell. Those who boast about wealth and youth, transgress the limit, those who are impure and fraudulent are punished with the hell called Krsna; one who cuts trees wantonly-goes to Asipatravana hell. The shepherds, hunters of deer go to Vahmijvala hell and so also those who apply fire to the unbaked vessels; A violator of vow one who goes astray from the rules of one’s Asrama — both of them fall into the hell called Sandamsayatana. Students who sleep during the day and those who are taught Vedas by their sons fall into Svabarjana hell.

4.41.36

Although the city of Bhogavati is well known in Rasatala, it should be known that there is in the region of Vasuki a city called Bhogavati like Janasthana of Ravana. What is to be noted is ‘As Agastya lives in the stellar region in the house constructed by Visvakarma enclosed by Kanjara mount he lives on the Southern part of Panchavati namely Malaya.

4.42.46

Savarni-Meru is different from Mahameru which is in the north of Kailasa. This Savarni Meru is in the extreme west of the mountains Pariyatra, Vajra, Chakravan and Meghaparvata.

Uttarakuru 4.43.1-52

Bhismaparva describes Uttarakuru to Dhrtarashtra ‘Oh, king! there exists the holy Uttarakuru inhabited by the Siddhas to the south of Nila mountain and north of Meru. There are trees perennially full of flowers and fruits. The flowers are fragrant and fruits are juicy. There are others called kshiris which ooze out milk and nectar of six kinds of taste. The earth of Uttarakurukhanda is replete with gems. The subtle sand particles are of gold. The place is delightful in all seasons and without mires. All those falling from heaven take birth here as human beings who are good-looking and are associated with the pious. Generally twins are born here. Girl babies are as beautiful as nymphs. The male and female babies born simultaneously will grow together and possess same form, qualities and dresses like the two worthy Chakravaka birds. The people here live without diseases and always with pleasant mind. Their life span is 11,000 years. There are birds called Bharunda with sharp and strong beaks. They carry the dead-bodies with their beaks and throw them into the caves.

Kings encourage & reward subordinates to achieve their objective 4.43.53-62; 4.44.1-7

Duryodhana in Udyogaparva praised Bhisma: Like the Sun among luminaries, the moon among planets, Kubera among Yaksas, Indra among among Maruts, Meru among mountains, Suparna (Garuda) among birds, Kumara (Skanda) among gods, Agni among Vasus, you are our commander-in-chief. We follow you like cows following the bull.

Leadership 4.44.11-17

When Angada, the heir-apparent, superintendent of the army is present it is not proper to hand over the signet ring to Hanuman.

It is expounded in Udyoga that plurality of leadership fails to achieve the object. There were three castes on one side and kshatriyas on the other. Time and again the three castes were divided in the fight that ensued and the kshatriyas became victorious. Then the brahmanas inquired the kshatriyas about the reason. The kshatriyas, the knowers of dharma, told them the truth of the matter — ‘We listen to the words of a single wise-man whereas you all follow your own wisdom severally. Then the brahmanas appointed one brahmana as a commander-in-chief who is brave and well-versed in state craft and eventually defeated the kshatriyas.

Angada not trusted by Vanaras 4.44.12-15

Angada is not reliable whereas because of being faithful minister (to Sugriva) Hanuman is reliable. Therefore it is proper to entrust the work to the latter. For, kings should neither totally disbelieve nor excessively believe. Both are damaging.

Rajadharma: ‘Excessive and exclusive trust is the destroyer of dharma and artha and distrust everywhere excels even death. Trust is untimely death. Keeping trust in a person lands one into trouble.

Rajadharma: ‘A king must always apprehend danger from relatives as from death. So a king must feign trust though distrusting’.

Even though Angada was not trustworthy why was he neither killed nor deserted? Relatives must be protected.

In Udyoga, Vidura says desertion is not right. By the desertion of brothers like Vibhisana, Sugriva, Dharmaputra in relation to Ravana, Vali and Suyodhana, There is loss of kingdom, life etc.

Rajadharma: ‘By dissension groups get destroyed. 0, Kesava! you are a leader of the group. Do what needs to be done as leader so that the group does not perish’. Vidura too in Udyogaparva - ‘Estranged from relatives they do not get sleep even on mattresses; they cannot be happy with their wives or women. They cannot evince interest in eulogy; cannot digest palatable words; their well-being cannot remain for long. Destruction is only the last resort to them’.

Prabodhacandrodaya: ‘Anger born of enmity burns up the family totally (without any remnant); Like fire produced out of friction between trees swayed by the forceful wind consumes the entire forest. Therefore, relatives must not be hated. They with or without qualities must necessarily be protected’.

As in Udyoga — ‘A single tree though big with many branches and strongly rooted can be forcefully crushed in a second by the wind. But those trees rooted in clusters by mutual support (togetherness) can withstand the forceful onslaught. Kinsmen like charcoals separated let out smoke; united, they burn’.

In Vanaparva Duryodhana and others although enemies captured by the Gandharvas were released by the Pandavas.

4.46.1-13

It is Mayavi, son of Dundubhi as already said in canto 9.4.

Remembering gods 4.46.1-24

Hanuman before leaping across the ocean remembered gods and others in Sundarakanda.

The sage Dhaumya consoling the dispirited Pandavas tells them - ‘listen to the descriptions of the mountains, holy places and the hermitages occupied by the brahmanas. Listening to them you would be griefless’. Markandeya Purana says, ‘A person who on a journey remembers Prthu, Arjuna, Bharata (son of Sakuntala), Nala and Rama shall be granted wealth and victory’.

Bhisma in Sreyodhyaya of Anusasanaparva — ‘If a person recites prayer to the gods together with the lineages of sages in three twilights all his sins done through sensory and motor organs knowingly or unknowingly during day-night times will be removed.

Suryasiddhanta and Bhismaparva extol the knowledge of geography.

4.46.25

The commentator opines that before achieving a bigger task like the killing of a stronger enemy, competence has to be acquired either by penance or visit to holy places, singing, listening, seeing or remembering the glory of a king, god, Brahma or a holy place. Vamana (a dwarf) though the Lord of the universe could subdue the sovereign king Bali only by performing rigorous penance.

In Vanaparva Jayadratha desirous of defeating the Pandavas propitiated Lord Paramesvara. Deserted Amba performed severe penance to kill Bhisma. It is narrated in Ambakhyana in Udyogaparva.

Maya 4.51.1-19

Is not the architect of asuras immortal? How can he be slain? The answer is this: How can Maya be immortal and everlasting when the person occupying the position of Indra himself is not? He, who attained the status of the architect of demons, got the title Maya. As the appellation, Indra is, so is that of Maya.

A question arises: Why did Brahma choose Hema, when the demon who loved her was killed by Indra, king of the gods? In fact, Maya was a devotee of Brahma. Then, were not Hiranya and Ravana devotees of Brahma? No, their case was different. Having perpetrated sins, they got destroyed. Maya was free of sins.

4.51.15

The commentator argues that since Maya, the great architect of the demons, is immortal how can he be killed? But then whosoever becomes the architect of the demons is called Maya. It is only a status and not the name of a demon. Therefore it is not a mistake as the maxim is ‘The status of Indra is like a stream’. Brahma gifts this garden and the dwelling to Hema in whose company Maya enjoyed the garden. This demonstrates that the word Brahma does not refer to the demon, only because he had the skill to create a variety of things.

The month of search of Sita 4.53.9

Kalasankyavyavasthitah relates to the bright half of the month of Margasira (month following Kartika). Probably there was Ksayamasa of Pushya month when two Sankramanas happen.

Hence it is during the bright half of Magha that the mango trees bloom. On seeing the mango blooms Rama was apprehensive that spring was not far off. Kataka and other commentaries interpret that Pushya month was the time limit for the search for Sita. Asvayuja relates to the end of Kartika, which was about to begin. ‘Kalasankhya’ refers to the next part of Kartika and messengers were sent to bring the monkeys before fifteen nights expire. Then all the vanaras returned at the end of the bright half of the month of Margasirsa. On the first day of Pushya the monkeys set out in search of Sita. There when some days in the dark half of Magha passed off these words were spoken. It is clear that after Sita was abducted only twelve months were left to keep Sita under custody.

Intellect, strength and virtue 4.54.1-2

Angada was endowed with eight limbs of intellect, four kinds of army and fourteen qualities. The limbs are desire to listen to what is to be listened to, listening, understanding of the meaning, retention of comprehended meaning, cogitating on pros and cons of the nature of meaning, considering the sense through arguments, giving up the fallacious and then the determination of the nature of an entity. Kautilya says, ‘desire to listen, listening, understanding and retention, removal of doubts and consolidation of the concept are the qualities of intellect’.

Kamandaka says, ‘Desire to listen, lightening, grasping, retention, arguments and counter, comprehension of sense and knowledge of truth are the attributes of intellect’. ‘Arthavijnana’ may be applicable to both intellect and army consisting of eight limbs. Limbs of the army are elephants, horses, deadly weapons/ missiles, ramparts, sword and other weapons, chariots, infantry and finance’.

Nitisastra says, ‘A king equipped with elephants, horses, machines, fences, weapons, chariots, infantry and wealth’ can conquer the earth. He should have four kinds of strength (force) —ministers, traders, foresters and servants, or strength of arms, mental strength, strength of expedients and strength of kinsmen, Or five kinds of strength: arms, minister, wealth , heredity and intellect.

The fourteen qualities are, ‘knowledge of place and time, resoluteness, forbearance, understanding, dexterity, energy secret counselling / consultation, keeping promises, prowess, competence, gratefulness, compassion towards those who have surrendered, indignation and steadiness’.

Hanuman expounds Angara’s qualities 4.54.1-3

Angada had eight essential qualities of a king which are Susrusa, desire to listen, Svana, listening, Cjrahana, understanding what others say, Dharma, retaining in mind what is understood, Uha, guessing intelligently, apoha, rejecting the unreasonable, Arthavijnanam, correct knowledge of the affairs of the state and tadvijnanam, knowledge of those that know.

Angada had four powers viz., the power of arms, mind, techniques and relatives or the four powers are the four means, Sama, Dana, Bhedha and Danda. He had the fourteen qualities — knowledge of place and time, firmness of mind, endurance of pain, knowledge of all things, efficiency, strength, keeping the secrets of political divisions, not contradicting oneself, valour, recognizing others’ strength, gratitude, affection for those that take refuge, steadfastness, and intolerance of injustice.

Siromani, Angada’s qualities 4.54.2-4

Angada is endowed with eight virtues such as inclination to hear, listening to others, grasping capacity, retention, reasoning in favour of proposition, reasoning against proposition, insight into meaning, and true wisdom. He is equipped with four-fold strength like sama or reconciliation, dana or gift, bheda or dissention, and nigraha or use of force. He possesses fourteen qualities, such as knowledge of place and time, firmness, bearing of distress, knowledge of profane matters, skillfulness, energy, keeping secrets, not violating one’s promise, heroism, knowledge of one’s strength, gratitude, protection of refugee, impatience, and steadiness.

Angada’s strength 4.54.2-4

‘Astangaya refers to eight qualities of Astagunaya buddhya’.These are desire to listen, listening with attention, grasping what is said, sustaining the purport, reasoning for and against, understanding with insight and wisdom derived from it’. Caturbalam is four kinds of strength, that is, persuasion, offering, dissension and punishment. Angada is described as Astangya and having Chaturbalam.

The fourteen virtues of Angada are awareness of time and place, firmness, ability to bear misfortune, knowledge, integrity, physical energy, secret counseling, non-contradicting other’s views, valour, appreciation of loyalty, gratitude and steadiness.

Four expedients to achieve success 4.54.3-6

Here are four expedients — Sama, dana, bheda and danda. Kamandaka mentions seven expedients, ‘conciliation, gift, dissension and chastisement disguise, connivance and black magic.

In Kamandaka ‘speech which does not cause anxiety is termed as Sama’’ and it is of five kinds — mutual help, eulogy of qualities, mention of relations, disclosure of the object in future and establishment of one’s view.

The Kauravas, haters of Sama were soon destroyed. The milky ocean churned by Sama by gods and demons was fruitful.

Bhedopaya is of three kinds — cutting through affection, generating quarrel and producing fear. In Kamandaka too ‘‘Bheda is of three types —removing affection, producing friction and fear.

Kamandaka : ‘Both Sama and Bheda must precede Dana.

In Kamandaka : ‘Danda is said to be of two kinds, open and secret.

Maya is deception. It is of two kinds — human and divine. Both are mentioned by Kamandaka — ‘Human deception consists of men hiding in the perforated pillars and icons and men assuming guises of women and showing some wondrous things in the night and assuming the forms of goblins, ghosts and gods etc. Assuming forms at will, showering weapons, fire-missiles, stones and water, disappearing in darkness are the divine deception. Bhima killed Kicaka taking the guise of a woman; Nala was in disguise (as a charioteer Bahuka to the king Rtuparna) by divine deception for a longer period’.

Hanuman’s strategy to motivate Angada 4.54.6-11

Seeing Angada disinclined to Sugriva’s task, Hanuman adopted the device of bheda or dissention, and set the monkeys favouring Angada at variance. He, then, used danda or force threatening the latter with eloquent words.

Hanuman dissuades Angada 4.54.6-12

Hanuman attempted to dissuade Angada from dejection by sayingthatthe monkeys would not tolerate him as king if they were separated from their wishes and children. Jambavan, Nila and ,Suhotra would not follow him and it was not possible to draw away the monkeys from Sugriva even by force, Even being against Sugriva is not correct for a weak, person, finally Hanuman tells Angada that even the Rikshabala’ fort which Angada thinks would be able to protect him was easily breakable by the arrows of Lakshmana. Sugriva issued orders for searching Sita not out of the fear of adharma, but out of fear of Lakshamana (54-6). Hanuman tried to put courage in Angada to make him act.

Six modes of foreign policy 4.54.12

A weak king cannot fight against a strong enemy. The six modes of foreign policy/royal policy are — Sadgunya; bearing of troops or standing firm so as to repel a charge, peace-Sandhi; War- Vigraha, expedition- Yana, halt-Asanaaa, seeking shelter-Samsraya and duplicity dvaidhibhava. Therefore, in respect of the enemy of equal strength or less strength Kamandaka suggests halt after war — ‘use of mutual force is termed as halt after war. After battling the enemy repulsion is termed as Asana or halting.’

Excellences necessary for a king 4.55.1-22

Excellences in a King

**\[A\]**  The eight virtues:

- 1\. Inclination to hear what others say
- 2\. Actually listening to what others say
- 3\. The capacity to grasp the meaning intended
- 4\. Keeping it firmly in one’s memory
- 5\. Putting forth reasoning in favour of a proposition
- 6\. Reasoning against a proposition
- 7\. Insight into other’s statements
- 8\. True wisdom

**\[B\]**  The Four-fold strength:

- 1\. Persuasion
- 2\. Gratification
- 3\. Sowing seeds of dissension in the ranks of enemies and
- 4\. Use of violence Wisdom lies in the use of these expedients.

**\[C\]**  The fourteen excellences:

- **1.**  A sense of time and place
- **2.**  Firmness
- **3.**  The capacity to endure hardship
- **4.**  Knowledge of all empirical subjects
- **5.**  Adroitness
- **6.**  Ardor
- **7.**  The capacity to guard one’s secrets
- **8.**  Consistency
- **9.**  Heroism
- **10.**  Knowing one’s strength as also that of enemy
- **11.**  Appreciation of other’s help
- **12.**  According protection to a fugitive
- **13.**  Indignation
- **14.**  Steadiness

Vanaras’ fear of their survival 4.56.14—16

The vanaras doubted their survival after Jatayu’s slaughter, Dasaratha’s death and Sita’s abduction. They think, if Jatayu had not died, if Sita had not been abducted, if Dasaratha wou Id be alive, it would be possible for Rama to come back. Jatayu obtained a higher existence by fighting with Ravana and dying in the presence îf Rama. Since the vanaras were not in the presence of Rama, and that they could not see Sita also, they think their life is fruitless. This made them grieve in desperation and they decided to fast unto death.

Sampati’s narration 4.58.35

Kataka Says: “Every word in this narration has significance. But the word ‘Svargatau’ has no relevance. The episode of Indra, too, is irrelevant. ‘Desirous of victory’ - is not appropriate. For, there was no desire to conquer one another. It would have been enough if it was stated - ‘We reached the Sun and when the Sun came to the meridian, my brother felt terribly tormented.’ The rest of it is unnecessary, irrelevant.” (Madhava Yogin)

Indra sends food to Sita while at Asokavanam 4.62.9

Sage Nishkara tells Sampati that Indrat (the person sent by Indra) will provide food for Sita and informs Sita that Rama would arrive and take her. She should live on the food, which would sustain her over a long period of one year so that the mission of gods is fulfilled. ‘Even gods cannot survive without food while in human form’. The question is, ‘was it not possible to live in Tretayuga during which life existed even in skeletons.

Then when one is weak, the bodily form changes (gets emaciated). The interpretation is, Ravana’s love for Sita may diminish if she gets emaciated and on account of which his merit may not be reduced. Then Ravana cannot be killed. Therefore in order that Sita’s beauty is not lost giving her food may not entail sin. Moreover Ravana had to believe that Sita is a human being and thinking that she is living on forest food although she was not taking the food offered by him and takes her to be as beautiful as before. If he thought she looked as before even without food and therefore she was not a human being then Rama could not kill Ravana. Therefore the theory that in Tretayuga one cannot live without food is refuted.

Abhjjidavhi mukah 4.63.15

It means waiting for the holy time of Abhijit. It is said in astrology that the fourth lagna counting from the Sun is Abhijit and this Abhijit muhurta removes all blemishes and it is very desirable for performing auspicious rituals.

4.64.3

Kataka says that some commentators compare the sea to a mirror, a reflection of the universe. But how can blue waters of the ocean reflect and how can waters with rising waves be the level surface of a mirror?

4.64.10

Udyogaparva says victory follows energy — ‘(A king) who is vigilant will never grieve in times of peril, rather, he endeavours. He endures pain for some time. A king of self-restraint and one who bears the burden will be victorious over the enemies’.

4.64.12

In Udyogaparva, Duryodhana addresses Bhisma as equal to Sukracarya (preceptor of demons) and asks him to become chief commander, like Aditya, to the luminaries, the Moon to plants, Kubera to Yakshas, Vasava to Maruts, Meru to mountains and Garuda to birds.

Visadoyam no sahate 4.64.12

‘Visadocyam no sahate’ one who is disturbed by desperation when the time for exhibition of valour comes, will not gain any ‘ Purushartha’ and because his brightness will be lost.

The monkeys were capable of jumping across limitless yojanas. Why did they keep guiet when the guestion of jumping across the sea, which is only a hundred yojanas was raised? "They kept guiet because they had fear of exceeding the time limit set by Sugriva whose order had never been broken. Another reason was they had become aware of the unimaginable might of Ravana. \|t has been said in Skandapurana that ‘Nila, Hanuman, Angada and Jambavan came to the sea shore, but were not able to move even a step, knowing the strength of Ravana’.

Vanaras express their difficulty to cross hundred yojanas 4.65.3-5

The statement that Vanaras had limited strength is not true. The vanara leaders had announced in the presence of Sugriva My power is not curtailed either on the earth or in the sky or on the mountains or in the gardens or even in the centre of the nether world’. in the previous sarga, Angada had also told the vanara leaders “None of you have an obstacle wherever it may be in this world. O best of monkeys, tell me who has the ability to go to Lanka?”

If it is so why did the vanaras say they could not jump over a hundred yojanas? \|t is because even though the vanaras had immense power, they thought access to the city of Lanka and to Sita is a difficult proposition. \|n their opinion, Hanuman was the hero who could achieve that great feat? To encourage him they talked that way expressing their inability.

Importance of encouragement 4.66.3-7

In Udyogaparva Brhaspati addressed Indra hidden in a hole of lotus stalk, running away from the fear of Nahusa’s power. Brhaspati along with gods, sages and Gandharvas went to Indra and eulogized him for his past deeds. Praised by Brhaspati, Indra slowly grew up and obtained the body endowed with strength’. In Karnaparva Krishna tells Arjuna: ‘Who other than the Pandavas with white horses and the banner of monkey can defeat the Kauravas who have come together. When you (Partha) are powerful to win over the three worlds of gods, demons and humans what to speak of the Kaurava army?

Name of Hanuman 4.66.21-24

A question arises: How a newly born child, Hanuman thought that it was a ripe, red fruit and it was fit to be tasted? The answer is the newly born child comes out ready to drink the breast-milk. It is a god-given instinct. For a monkey-child, a desire to taste a ripe fruit like mango might be a god-given instinct, says Kataka. Hanu = Chin, Hanuman = One who possesses a wounded chin.

Kinds of sons 4.66.29

Manu: ‘Aurasa, Ksetraja, Datta, Krtrima, Gudhotpanna, Apaviddha these six sons store paternal property and are also the relatives who have rights to offer libations of water. Kanina, Sahodha, Krita, Paunarbhava, Svayamdatta and Savdra are the sons who have rights to offer libations of water but do not have proprietary rights.

Aurasa is a son begotten by a wedded woman in accordance with the rites. Ksetrajna is a son begotten through a wife by the permission of the husband. Niyoga is dead /diseased /impotent without an issue. Dattaka is a son given over with love in the adverse circumstance by mother /father. Krtrima is a son who can discriminate between merits and demerits. Gudhotpanna is a son who is given birth to in a house but one does not know to whom he is born, his birth is hidden in respect of his father. Apaviddha is a son who is received by a person when deserted by the parents or by one of the two. A maiden in her paternal house may beget a son secretly. The son is known as Kanina and belongs to the person whom she weds. A maiden whose state of pregnancy known or unknown, is wedded to a person and the son born from her womb is called Sahodha son and he belongs to the husband. A son is called Kritaka who is bought by a person for the sake of progeny from the parents whether or not of the same caste. A woman left by her husband or a widow or by self-will taking another as her husband begets a son he is called Paunarbhava. Without parents or left by parents without reason if a son offers himself to another man he is called Svayamdatta son with respect to the other man. Saudra / Parasava is a son born to a Brahmana and Sudra woman out of desire. He is Parasava because he is as good as dead while alive. A father without a son while giving his daughter in marriage performs the rite making the son born to his daughter as the one who would do all the religious acts. In the days of yore Daksaprajapati in order to propagate his lineage did perform this ritual’.

In Kaliyuga the acceptance of a son other than Datta and Aurasa is prohibited. However, in Candrikasmrtyarthasana and other works ‘the acceptance of others as son is considered under Kaliyugadharma'’.

Hanuman crosses the ocean 4.66.38

Since Hanuman’s body was under control, expanding or reducing the body is not impossible for him. When Jambavan referred to the prowess of the monkeys it was only to show the higher prowess that Hanuman possessed. That was a divine opportunity provided to Hanuman when he was reminded of his own prowess. In fact, the monkeys who went in the other three directions also knew how to fly. Since there were mountains at every twenty or thirty yojanas there may not be difficulty in crossing over the ocean as one can rest on the mountains during flight. But the ocean which was a hundred yojanas at a stretch is difficult. The mountains that exist in this area however have been submerged by the demons so that one cannot cross the sea. Even the boats were submerged and, therefore, Sugriva made no mention of it. Hence there is a reference to those who went in the eastern direction as ‘those who go by mountains or boats.

4.67.4

Apastamba says, ‘self-praise and censure of others must be shunned’. Hanuman’s is a heroic speech and hence it is not a blemish.
